## §2 UCP Advertising support

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.company-profile-https` The Company's UCP profile is at `https://{organization.domain}/.well-known/ucp`, where UCP puts it (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L7) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.document-speaks-domain` The document that speaks for the domain (spec 10.3) and the UCP profile are on the same host _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L8) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-offers-sign` A Company that offers sign-in has an issuer (spec 3.2), found from the protected resource metadata at `https://{organization.domain}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L9) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.extension-personal-agent` For this extension, the Personal Agent selects the issuer as spec 3.2 describes, including `auth.issuer` when that document lists more than one authorization server, and the Company's UCP services SHOULD support account access through that issuer [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L10) | SHOULD | both |  |
| → | `ucp.service-requires-different` If a UCP service requires a different issuer, the Personal Agent MUST NOT use that issuer through this extension [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L11) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.account-access-through` Account access through this extension is unavailable for that service, though UCP used independently may still offer it (below) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L12) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-offers-sign-2` A Company that offers no sign-in can offer UCP signed out without an issuer (spec 3.2), and one that sets `auth.disabled` offers UCP signed out to Personal Agents too _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L13) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.identity-linking-stays` Its UCP identity linking stays available to UCP used independently of this extension (below) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L14) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.support-means-company` Support means that the Company's UCP services, at the endpoints its profile lists, are endpoints this extension defines: the Personal Agent sends them the Session header (spec 5.2), and the Company handles its requests as UCP defines (4, 8) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L15) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.personal-agent-supports` A Personal Agent that supports this extension SHOULD declare `"ucp";v="1"` in `Poppy-Extensions` (spec 3.4), so a Company can tell from its other requests that the Personal Agent speaks UCP, for example to point it to UCP from another of its interfaces [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L16) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.company-rely-declaration` A Company doesn't rely on the declaration: it recognizes a UCP request from the request itself (spec 3.3), which names the Personal Agent's UCP platform profile (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.personal-agent-support` A Personal Agent that doesn't support this extension ignores the entry and uses the Company's `agent`, `apis`, and `web` as the specification describes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L18) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `ucp.company-list-endpoint` A Company MAY also list its UCP MCP endpoint in `apis`, for MCP clients that speak UCP but don't know this extension [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L19) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `ucp.tools-requires-personal` The tools there are UCP's: UCP requires the Personal Agent to advertise its platform profile on every request, in the form the transport defines (3), so a client that does gets UCP's tools, and one that doesn't gets UCP's `invalid_profile_url` error rather than a result _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L20) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.without-extension-company` UCP without this extension. A Company MUST NOT require a UCP platform to implement this protocol as a condition of access UCP otherwise permits [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L21) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ucp.software-implements-protocol` Software that implements this protocol MAY also use UCP with the Company independently of this extension, with any mechanism UCP permits, such as the Accelerated IdP Flow [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L22) | MAY | both |  |

| ! | `issuer.company-offers-sign` A Company that offers sign-in MUST have an OAuth issuer [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L41) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-publishes-metadata` If the Company publishes this metadata, its `resource` MUST be exactly `https://{organization.domain}`, and its `authorization_servers`, when nonempty, names the issuer: [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L42) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.http-valid-metadata` HTTP 404, or valid metadata with `authorization_servers` absent or empty, means the Company has no issuer _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L43) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.valid-auth-issuer` This is valid only when `auth.issuer` is absent and the Company offers no sign-in _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L44) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `issuer.personal-agent-domain` A Personal Agent MUST NOT use the domain fallback after a timeout, another error status, invalid metadata, or a failure to verify an issuer [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L45) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `issuer.fall-back-company` It MUST NOT fall back for a Company whose issuer it already knows unless a successful discovery explicitly establishes that the issuer was removed [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L46) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.lists-authorization-server` If it lists one authorization server, that is the Company's issuer. `auth.issuer` is optional, and if present MUST name that server (3.1) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L47) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.lists-more-company` If it lists more than one, such as one for the Company's employees, `auth.issuer` in `poppy.json` names the one Personal Agents use (3.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L48) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `issuer.9728-leaves-choice` RFC 9728 leaves the choice among them to the client, but User IDs and refresh tokens belong to one issuer (5.1), so every Personal Agent has to choose the same one _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L49) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `issuer.personal-agent-start` A Personal Agent MUST NOT start Direct, Device, or Mediated Sign-In with a Company that sets it [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L50) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `issuer.company-sets-auth` A Company that sets `auth.disabled` MUST NOT list the Mediated Sign-In extension or `signed_in` access (below) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L51) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `issuer.without-verifying-client` It MAY do so without verifying the client assertion (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L52) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `issuer.changes-personal-agents` If it changes, Personal Agents MUST use new User IDs, Agent IDs, and Sessions for the new identifier [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `issuer.earlier-carts-conversations` Earlier carts and conversations do not transfer automatically _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L54) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `issuer.several-domains-same` Several domains MAY have the same issuer, such as a Company with a domain for each country, and they are then one Company: the same User IDs (5.1), Sessions, and refresh tokens apply to all of them [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L55) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-select-same` The Company MUST select that same issuer on each domain (above) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L56) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-give-scope` The Company MUST give each scope the same authorization meaning across these domains [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L57) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-publish-same` The Company SHOULD publish the same scope descriptions and hints across these domains [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L58) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `issuer.expose-different-scopes` MAY expose different scopes or capabilities [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L59) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `issuer.other-fields-differ` Other fields MAY differ by domain, such as the APIs or the website, and the Personal Agent uses the document of the domain it is working with [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L60) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.issuer-represent-exactly` An issuer MUST represent exactly one Company [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L61) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.provider-hosts-several` A provider that hosts several Companies MUST give each its own issuer, such as `https://auth.provider.example/shop-a`, even when they share servers [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L62) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.issuer-publish-oauth` The issuer MUST publish OAuth Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414), at the URL RFC 8414 §3.1 defines [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L63) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.protected-resources-9728` Its `protected_resources` (RFC 9728 §4) MUST list `https://{domain}` for every domain whose issuer it is, with no path, port, or trailing slash [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L64) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `issuer.list-other-resources` It MAY list other resources too, such as the Company's MCP servers [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L65) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.before-using-company` Before using a Company's `poppy.json`, the Personal Agent fetches the metadata and MUST check that its `issuer` exactly matches the issuer it found, character for character [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L66) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.check-protected-resources` It MUST also check that `protected_resources` includes `https://{organization.domain}`, compared as RFC 9728 §3.3 describes after lowercasing the host, as RFC 3986 §6.2.2.1 allows (3.1) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L67) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.issuer-protected-resources` `issuer` and `protected_resources`, which it checks against `poppy.json` (above) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L68) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.token-endpoint-issues` `token_endpoint` issues access and refresh tokens (4.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L69) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.revocation-endpoint-revokes` `revocation_endpoint` revokes refresh tokens (4.6) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L70) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.grant-types-supported` `grant_types_supported` lists the grant types the token endpoint accepts _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L71) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.required-include-refresh` Required, and it MUST include `refresh_token` (4.4) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L72) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.says-direct-device` It also says which of Direct and Device Sign-In the Company offers (4): `authorization_code` for Direct Sign-In and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` for Device Sign-In _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L73) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.authorization-endpoint-starts` `authorization_endpoint` starts Direct Sign-In (4.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L74) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.required-grant-types` Required if `grant_types_supported` includes `authorization_code` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L75) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.device-authorization-endpoint` `device_authorization_endpoint` starts Device Sign-In (4.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L76) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.required-grant-types-2` Required if `grant_types_supported` includes `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L77) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.scopes-supported-lists` `scopes_supported` lists the scopes the issuer supports, as RFC 8414 §2 defines _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L78) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-offers-sign-2` A Company that offers sign-in SHOULD list every scope a Personal Agent can request here, in `scopes_supported` of its protected resource metadata (above), or in both (4.7) [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L79) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.token-endpoint-auth` `token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported` lists the signing algorithms the token endpoint accepts for client assertions, as RFC 8414 §2 defines (4.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L80) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.describe-support-delegation` It does not describe support for delegation signatures at resource endpoints (5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L81) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `issuer.metadata-other-fields` The metadata MAY have other fields, which Personal Agents ignore [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L82) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `issuer.account-access-advance` Account access in advance. A `poppy` entry in `agent.protocols` MAY have `access` set to `session` (the default) or `signed_in`. `signed_in` says the interface requires account access before useful work can begin, so the Personal Agent can arrange sign-in before its first request [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L83) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.company-lists-signed` A Company that lists `signed_in` MUST have an issuer [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L84) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.auth-disabled` MUST NOT set `auth.disabled` [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L85) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `issuer.personal-agents-ignore` Personal Agents MUST ignore unknown values and handle them as an absent hint [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L86) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §3.3 Extensions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `discovery.plain-names-without` Plain names, without a domain, are reserved for extensions defined with this protocol _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L89) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.anyone-else-start` Anyone else MUST start an extension's name with a domain they control, such as `example.com/gift-wrap` [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L90) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.entry-version-extension` Each entry has a `version`, the extension's major version _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L91) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.changes-implementations-safely` Changes that implementations can safely ignore keep the version, and incompatible changes get a new one _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L92) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.extension-defines-entry` Each extension defines the entry's other fields for each of its versions _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L93) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.personal-agent-declares` A Personal Agent declares the extensions it uses with a Company, one version of each, in the `Poppy-Extensions` header (3.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L94) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.need-declare-extension` It doesn't need to declare an extension that the Company recognizes from the request itself, such as one that defines its own grant type _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L95) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `extensions.ignore-unknown` Personal Agents and Companies MUST ignore extensions and versions they don't support and fields they don't recognize, so either side can work with the other under this specification alone [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L96) | MUST | both | `extensions/ignore-unknown` |
| ! | `discovery.extension-define-content` An extension can define content for conversation messages, which they carry in `extensions` (8.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L97) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.extension-publish-json` The extension MUST publish a JSON Schema for that content [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L98) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `discovery.company-refuse-request` A Company MAY refuse a request it handles only with an extension that the request doesn't declare, in a version the Company lists, unless the request itself uses the extension [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L99) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `discovery.returns-extension-required` It returns `extension_required` (HTTP 403) with the extension's name in `extension`, in a JSON body, both at APIs and at endpoints this protocol or an extension defines _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L100) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.access-token-error` It isn't an access token error, so it doesn't go in `WWW-Authenticate` (section 7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L101) | MUST | both |  |

## §3.4 Versions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `discovery.supported-versions-https` Each URL in `supported_versions` MUST be an HTTPS URL on the host that served `poppy.json`, after any redirects [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L104) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `discovery.personal-agent-document` The Personal Agent MUST NOT use a document whose URL is on another host [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L105) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.follow-redirect` MUST NOT follow a redirect from it [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L106) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `discovery.otherwise-domain-poppy` Otherwise any domain's `poppy.json` could link to a file someone uploaded to a Company's domain and have it speak for that Company _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L107) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `discovery.document-protocol-version` The document there has the `protocol_version` it is listed under, and no `supported_versions` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L108) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `discovery.personal-agent-protocol` The Personal Agent MUST NOT use it if its `protocol_version` is another one [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L109) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `discovery.path-anything-unlike` Its path can be anything, unlike `poppy.json`'s (section 3), because `poppy.json` names it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L110) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.every-document-company` Every document a Company serves at the same time MUST have the same `organization.domain` and select the same issuer (3.2), so that a new version doesn't change the Company's identifier, and with it User IDs and refresh tokens [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L111) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `discovery.other-fields-differ` Other fields MAY differ by version [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L112) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.versions-compatible-same` Two versions are compatible when they have the same major version and, before 1.0, the same minor version _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L113) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `discovery.personal-agent-chooses` The Personal Agent chooses the newest version, among `protocol_version` and the versions in `supported_versions`, that is compatible with one it implements, and uses that version's document _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L114) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `discovery.none` If none is, it MUST NOT use any of them [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L115) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `discovery.personal-agent-send` The Personal Agent MUST send the same values on every request in a Session, and starts a new Session to change them [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L116) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `discovery.requests-without-session` Requests without the Session header, such as discovery and OAuth requests, don't carry these headers _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L117) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.checking-version-endpoint` Checking the version. An endpoint that verifies the Session header (5.3) MUST also check `Poppy-Version` [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L118) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `discovery.rejects-request-without` It rejects a request without it, or with a version that isn't compatible with one the Company serves, with `version_unsupported` (HTTP 400, JSON body), and MUST NOT handle the request under another version [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L119) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `discovery.company-plans-stop` A Company that plans to stop serving a version MAY say so in its responses to requests in that version, with the `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) and `Sunset` (RFC 8594) headers [↗](pap-0.4/03-discovery.md#L120) | MAY | company |  |

## §4 OAuth

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `oauth.some-servers-support` Some servers support them and some don't _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L7) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `oauth.personal-agents-read` Personal Agents read it from the same metadata as every other client, so it can list a grant the Company doesn't offer them _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L8) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `oauth.company-offers-sign` A Company that offers sign-in SHOULD offer Direct Sign-In [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L9) | SHOULD | company |  |
| → | `oauth.personal-agent-direct` A Personal Agent SHOULD use Direct Sign-In when the Company offers it [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L10) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4 Browser control Marking steps

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `bctl.data-poppy-user` \| `data-poppy-user-step` \| On \| The Personal Agent's browser \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L30) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `bctl.interaction-control-read` \| `interaction` \| A control \| Can read it. Leaves changing or activating it to the User. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L31) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.interaction-form-read` \| `interaction` \| A form \| Can read it. Leaves its controls, and submitting it, to the User. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L32) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.submission-form-fill` \| `submission` \| A form \| Can fill in its controls, unless other marks say not to. Leaves submitting it to the User. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L33) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.form-controls-ones` A form's controls are the ones it owns in HTML, including controls outside it that name it in their `form` attribute _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.control-inside-submission` A control inside a `submission` form can also be marked `interaction` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L35) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.marked-control-mark` A marked control doesn't mark the rest of its form _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L36) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.value-other-interaction` A value other than `interaction` or `submission`, or `submission` on anything but a form, counts as `interaction` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L37) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.company-mark-every` The Company SHOULD mark every control that performs the step, or the form it is in [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L38) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.mark-before-used` SHOULD mark them before they can be used [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L39) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.company-filling-submission` The Company SHOULD NOT let filling in a `submission` form perform the step itself [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L40) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.whatever-marks-company` Whatever it marks, the Company's servers MUST check the action's conditions themselves, because marks don't stop anything (8.1) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L41) | MUST | company |  |

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `mediated.company-needs-second` If the Company needs a second step, it sends the User a one-time code and returns a `code_required` error with a sign-in ID: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L26) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `mediated.correct-code-returns` A correct code returns the token response _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L27) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `mediated.wrong-code-returns` A wrong code returns `code_required` again, until the Company's attempt limit, and then `invalid_grant` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L28) | MUST | company |  |

## §4 UCP Identity and authorization

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.layer-spec-request` \| Layer (spec 1.1) \| On a UCP request \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L32) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.discovery-poppy-json` \| Discovery \| `poppy.json` leads to the UCP profile at `/.well-known/ucp` (3). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L33) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.operator-recognition-personal` \| Operator recognition \| The Personal Agent's operator signature, and its UCP platform profile named in `UCP-Agent`. In UCP's terms this is agent-authenticated access. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L34) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.sessions-session-header` \| Sessions \| The Session header. UCP's sessions are per workflow: a conversation, a cart, a checkout, an order, each with its own identifier and lifecycle, and a cart leads to a checkout leads to an order (8). There is no overarching UCP session. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L35) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.account-access-access` \| Account access \| An access token from the Company's issuer: UCP's user-authenticated access, through identity linking (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L36) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.platform-profile-advertisement` The platform profile advertisement, in the transport's form (3), naming the profile for the selected version, and the other request metadata UCP's binding requires, such as an idempotency key on requests that change state _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L37) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.where-transport-carries` Where a transport carries the profile in more than one place, the Personal Agent MUST send the same URL in each [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L38) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.company-reject-request` the Company MUST reject a request where they differ; otherwise a request could authenticate as one platform and negotiate as another [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L39) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.extends-identity-binding` This extends UCP's identity binding, which rejects a request whose authenticated identity conflicts with `UCP-Agent` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L40) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.poppy-session-session` `Poppy-Session`, the Session header, as on any endpoint this protocol or an extension defines (spec 5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L41) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.operator-signature-personal` An operator signature: the Personal Agent SHOULD sign UCP requests with an HTTP Message Signature, as spec 5.3 recommends for every request that carries the Session header [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L42) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.signature-serve-both` One signature can serve both protocols when it covers `poppy-session` and `authorization` for this protocol, and the request target, `content-digest`, `content-type`, `ucp-agent`, and `idempotency-key` for UCP, as UCP's identity resolution and signature rules describe _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L43) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.signing-published-platform` When the signing key is published in the platform profile's `keys`, a verified signature identifies the same profile the request negotiates with _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L44) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.algorithm-both-verifiers` The key's algorithm has to be one both verifiers accept _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.authorization-access-token` `Authorization`, with an access token, when signed in _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L46) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `ucp.company-verify-session` A Company MAY verify the Session header on UCP requests and use it, for example to recognize a returning signed-out User [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L47) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.verify-header-before` it MUST verify the header before relying on any Session claim, and a UCP service that uses no Session claims can ignore it (8) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L48) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-returns-token` The Company returns `token_type` `Bearer` for tokens for its UCP services, as spec 4.5 allows for a service that doesn't accept DPoP, for example for a `resource` that names them, and the Personal Agent sends each token as its `token_type` names _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L49) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.request-what-personal` \| Request \| What the Personal Agent sends \| What it gets \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L50) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.signed-session-header` \| Signed out \| The Session header; no access token \| What the Company offers without an account, as its UCP profile and access policy allow: catalog search and lookup, policies, Ask, carts, and guest checkout \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L51) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.signed-session-header-2` \| Signed in \| The Session header and an access token (spec 4.5) \| The same, personalized and extended by the token's scopes: search that reflects the User's preferences and entitlements, saved addresses and instruments in checkout, order history, and whatever else the Company's identity linking gates \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L52) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-offers-both` A Company that offers both this protocol's sign-in and identity linking makes them one: it MUST offer Direct Sign-In [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L53) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.list-private-issuer` MUST list `private_key_jwt` in its issuer's `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported`, so a Personal Agent can authenticate as spec 4.1 describes [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L54) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-list-scope` The Company MUST list each scope in its identity linking `config.scopes` in `scopes_supported`, as UCP requires [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L55) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.describe-scope-description` It SHOULD describe each scope in its UCP `description`, in `auth.scopes`, or in an OpenAPI description it lists [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L56) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.give-auth-scope` SHOULD give `auth.scope_hints` for it wherever the description is (spec 4.7) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L57) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.scopes-well-known` The scopes are UCP's: its well-known scopes, such as `dev.ucp.shopping.order:read` and `dev.ucp.common.ask:read`, and any the Company adds under UCP's rules _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L58) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.personal-agent-requests` The Personal Agent requests the scopes a task needs, from `config.scopes` for operations that require an account, and from the Company's other described scopes for ones that unlock more without being required, such as member pricing _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L59) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.request-made-independently` A request made independently of this extension doesn't carry the Session header, and its access is UCP's alone, as UCP defines (2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L60) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.personal-agent-send` A Personal Agent MUST NOT send a token it got independently of this extension on a request that carries the Session header [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L61) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.response-personal-agent` \| UCP response \| The Personal Agent \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L62) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.identity-required-error` \| `401` with `identity_required` and no `error` in the challenge \| Uses a refresh token that covers the scopes, or signs in for them, and retries (spec 5.4). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L63) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.error-invalid-token` \| `401` with `error="invalid_token"` \| Refreshes the access token (spec 4.4), or continues signed out if refresh fails (spec 5.5). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L64) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.insufficient-scope-full` \| `403` with `insufficient_scope` and the full required set in `scope` \| Uses a refresh token that covers the scopes if it has one. Otherwise it requests the scopes it lacks (below) and retries. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L65) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.identity-optional-messages` \| `identity_optional` in `messages` \| Tells the User what signing in would unlock, and signs in only if the User wants to. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L66) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.requesting-more-scopes` Requesting more scopes. For `insufficient_scope`, the Personal Agent follows UCP: it requests only the missing scopes, by incremental authorization, and doesn't start account linking over _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L67) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.company-offers-identity` A Company that offers identity linking MUST keep the scopes the User already granted when it grants the missing ones, so the new token covers both, including scopes for the Company's other APIs [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L68) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `ucp.extension-personal-agent-2` This extension doesn't use it: a Personal Agent signs in with Direct or Device Sign-In _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L69) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.1 Agent identity

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `identity.personal-agent-client` A Personal Agent's `client_id` MUST be an HTTPS URL that returns its metadata document [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L13) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `identity.client-equal-document` `client_id` MUST equal the URL the document was fetched from [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L14) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.jwks-https-same` `jwks_uri` MUST be an HTTPS URL on the same domain as `client_id` [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L15) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.contains-public-keys` The key set contains only public keys _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L16) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.sign-client-assertions` They sign client assertions, and the delegations that vouch for the keys that sign Session JWTs (5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.redirect-uris-lists` `redirect_uris` lists where Direct Sign-In may send the User back to (4.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L18) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.entry-https-same` Each entry MUST be an HTTPS URL on the same domain as `client_id`, or a loopback redirect URI for an app on the User's computer, as RFC 8252 §7.3 defines [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L19) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `identity.personal-agent-authenticates` The Personal Agent authenticates at the token endpoint with a client assertion signed by a key from `jwks_uri` (`private_key_jwt`, RFC 7523) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L20) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `identity.session-jwts-signed` Its Session JWTs are signed with delegated keys instead (5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L21) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.client-assertion-company` The client assertion's `aud` MUST be the Company's issuer, as a single string [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L22) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.companies-reject-client` Companies MUST reject a client assertion with any other `aud`, compared character for character, including their token endpoint URL [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `identity.follows-draft-ietf` This follows draft-ietf-oauth-rfc7523bis _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L24) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.endpoints-company-metadata` The endpoints in a Company's metadata aren't checked (3.2), so an `aud` set to an endpoint could name another Company's endpoint, and that Company would accept the assertion _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L25) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `identity.client-assertions-follow` Client assertions follow RFC 7523 §3 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L26) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `identity.personal-agent-make` The Personal Agent MUST make them short-lived [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L27) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `identity.include-unique-unguessable` MUST include `iat` and a unique, unguessable `jti` [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L28) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `identity.company-reject-reused` The Company MAY reject a reused `jti`, as RFC 7523 §3 allows [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L29) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `identity.companies-accept-client` Companies MUST accept client assertions signed with `ES256` [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L30) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `identity.accept-ones-signed` SHOULD accept ones signed with `PS384`. `PS384` lets a Personal Agent have its client assertions signed blindly (10.7) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L31) | SHOULD | company |  |

## §4.2 Direct Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `direct.redirect-exactly-match` `redirect_uri` MUST exactly match an entry in the Personal Agent's `redirect_uris` (4.1), except for the port of a loopback redirect URI, as RFC 8252 §7.3 describes [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `direct.redirect-back-carries` The redirect back carries the Company's issuer in `iss` (RFC 9207), including on `error=access_denied` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L35) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `direct.personal-agent-check` The Personal Agent MUST check that `iss` exactly matches the issuer of the Company it started sign-in with [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L36) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `direct.stops-response-another` This stops a response from another Company's sign-in being swapped in _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L37) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `direct.token-request-carries` The token request carries the Personal Agent's client assertion (4.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L38) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `direct.companies-offer-direct` Companies that offer Direct Sign-In, and Personal Agents that open the authorization URL on a device other than the one the User is using, MUST follow the best practices in RFC 10027 (BCP 247) §2, as for Device Sign-In (4.3) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L39) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `direct.personal-agent-receive` A Personal Agent SHOULD receive the redirect only on the device that opened the authorization URL when it can, at a loopback redirect URI or in its own app signed in as the User who started the sign-in (RFC 8252) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L40) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.3 Device Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `device.companies-offer-device` Companies that offer Device Sign-In and Personal Agents that use it MUST follow the best practices in RFC 10027 (BCP 247) §2 [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L43) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `device.personal-agent-shows` The Personal Agent shows the User `verification_uri` and `user_code`, or `verification_uri_complete` as a link or QR code _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L44) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `device.keeps-device-code` It keeps `device_code` private _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `device.before-showing-personal` Before showing them, the Personal Agent MUST check that the link's host is the host of the Company's issuer or `organization.domain` (3.1), or a subdomain of either [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L46) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `device.show-company-organization` MUST show the Company's `organization.name` and domain with them [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L47) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `device.otherwise-company-could` Otherwise a Company could pass off another Company's sign-in page as its own, and the User would approve a sign-in there for the Company that asked _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L48) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `device.opening-link-approve` Opening the link MUST NOT approve the request by itself [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L49) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `device.poll-carries-client` Each poll carries the client assertion _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L50) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `device.once-user-approves` Once the User approves, the poll returns the tokens in 4.7 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L51) | MUST | both |  |

## §4.4 Refresh tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `refresh.sign-returns-refresh` Sign-in returns a refresh token (RFC 6749, section 6), so the Personal Agent can get access tokens later without asking the User to sign in again _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L54) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `refresh.send-scope-fewer` It MAY send `scope` to ask for fewer scopes than the refresh token has, for example read-only access for a task that only looks things up, and `resource` for a token for one service (4.5) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L55) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `refresh.refresh-token-rotation` Refresh token rotation follows RFC 6749 §6: the Personal Agent uses a new refresh token if the response has one, and keeps the old one otherwise _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L56) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `refresh.refresh-token-tied` A refresh token isn't tied to a Session _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L57) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `refresh.user-sessions-access` Any of the User's Sessions can use access tokens from it (5.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L58) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `refresh.copied-refresh-token` A copied refresh token is useless without a client assertion from the Personal Agent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L59) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `refresh.personal-agent-signs` If the Personal Agent signs blindly, its other Users can get client assertions too, so it protects refresh tokens in other ways (10.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.5 Access tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tokens.personal-agents-support` Personal Agents SHOULD support DPoP, because a Personal Agent that doesn't can't sign in at a Company that requires it [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L63) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.personal-agent-dpop` The Personal Agent MUST use each DPoP key for one User ID only, for the same reason as delegated keys (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L64) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tokens.company-decides-token` The Company decides for each token whether to bind it, and returns `token_type` `Bearer` for one it doesn't bind, as RFC 9449 §5 allows, such as a token for a service that doesn't accept DPoP _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L65) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tokens.domain-metadata-finding` The domain's own metadata (3.2) is for finding the issuer, and doesn't make any service need its own tokens _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L66) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tokens.before-first-signed` Before its first signed-in call to an API or a conversation `endpoint`, the Personal Agent fetches the metadata at the URL RFC 9728 §3.1 defines from the service's URL (an MCP server's `url`, the URL in an OpenAPI description's `servers`, or the `endpoint`) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L67) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tokens.uses-metadata-resource` It uses the metadata only if its `resource` is the URL it derived the metadata URL from, as RFC 9728 §3.3 requires, and otherwise treats it as absent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L68) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tokens.metadata-exists-resource` If the metadata exists and its `resource` isn't `https://{organization.domain}`, the Personal Agent requests a token with `resource` set to it (RFC 8707), at sign-in or refresh, and uses that token only there _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L69) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tokens.otherwise-default-token` Otherwise the default token works there, as it does at the other endpoints this protocol defines _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L70) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tokens.company-accepts-token` The Company accepts a token issued for a `resource` only at that service, and returns `invalid_target` for a `resource` it doesn't serve _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L71) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tokens.service-gets-token` A service that gets a token not issued for it returns `invalid_token` with `resource_metadata` in its challenge (RFC 9728 §5.1), so a Personal Agent with stale metadata learns about it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L72) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.7 Scopes and token responses

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `scopes.scopes-supported-oauth` `scopes_supported` in the OAuth server metadata, in the protected resource metadata of the domain the Personal Agent is working with, or in both, lists the scopes the Company supports (3.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L75) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `scopes.personal-agent-uses` The Personal Agent uses the scopes in either list _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L76) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `scopes.request-scopes-documented` It MAY also request scopes documented by the Company's APIs or sign-in extensions, even when absent from both [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L77) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `scopes.either-list-leave` Either list MAY leave out scopes the Company offers only to its other clients [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L78) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `scopes.company-limit-scopes` the Company MAY limit the scopes it grants by client, as RFC 6749 §3.3 allows [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L79) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `scopes.company-describe-scope` The Company SHOULD describe each scope it offers Personal Agents, so the Personal Agent can choose the ones a task needs: in the scopes of an OAuth 2.0 security scheme in an OpenAPI description it lists (section 7), or otherwise in `auth.scopes` [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L80) | SHOULD | company |  |
| → | `scopes.both-describe-scope` When both describe a scope, the Personal Agent uses the description in `auth.scopes` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L81) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `scopes.company-give-hints` A Company MAY give hints about any scope in `auth.scope_hints`, so a Personal Agent can tell how consequential a scope is before requesting it [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L82) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `scopes.entry-keyed-scope` Each entry is keyed by scope name and describes the most consequential of the actions that require the scope, in two fields: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L83) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `scopes.personal-agent-ignore` A Personal Agent MUST ignore fields it doesn't recognize, and treat a `changes` value it doesn't recognize as `irreversible`, so later versions can add both [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L84) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.replace-descriptions-like` They don't replace descriptions, and like other content from a Company (10.1), they are its claims, not the User's approval _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L85) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `signin.scope-enforcement` Companies decide which actions require each scope and enforce them across APIs and actions performed by the Company Agent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L86) | MUST | company | `signin/partial-approval` |
| ! | `scopes.website-able-apply` A website may not be able to apply them _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L87) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `scopes.give-signed-browser` It can then give a signed-in browser the account's full access, and the Company and the User accept that through `poppy:browser-sign-in` (section 6) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L88) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `scopes.company-grant-scopes` The Company MUST NOT grant scopes beyond those requested [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L89) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `scopes.stricter-oauth-lets` This is stricter than OAuth, which lets a server grant other scopes (RFC 6749 §3.3), because the User approved only the scopes the Personal Agent asked for _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L90) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.sign-request-include` Each sign-in request MUST include `scope`, except where an extension continues an earlier request, as a space-separated string, following OAuth scope syntax [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L91) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `scopes.missing-unknown-scopes` Missing or unknown scopes are rejected with `invalid_scope` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L92) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `scopes.company-grant-fewer` The Company MAY grant fewer scopes than requested, for any reason RFC 6749 §3.3 allows, and the response's `scope` says which it granted [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L93) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `signin.least-scopes` A Personal Agent SHOULD request only the scopes the User's tasks need, following RFC 9700 §2.3 [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L94) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `scopes.task-needs-more` If a task needs more access than the refresh token allows, the User signs in again, and the Personal Agent requests every scope it still needs, including previously granted scopes it wants to keep, following RFC 6749 §3.3 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L95) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.request-missing-scopes` It does not request only the missing scopes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L96) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `scopes.refresh-token-replaces` The new refresh token replaces the old one, which the Personal Agent SHOULD revoke (4.6) [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L97) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.revoking-replaced-refresh` Revoking a replaced refresh token isn't sign-out (5.5) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L98) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `scopes.pending-failed-sign` A pending or failed sign-in leaves existing tokens unchanged _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L99) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `scopes.sign-returns-access` Sign-in returns an access token (4.5) and a refresh token _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L100) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `scopes.refresh-returns-access` Refresh (4.4) returns an access token and MAY return a replacement refresh token, as RFC 6749 §6 describes [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L101) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `scopes.6749-describes-response` As RFC 6749 §5.1 describes, the response leaves `scope` out only when the Company granted exactly the scopes requested _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L102) | MUST | company |  |

## §4.8 What Poppy adds to OAuth

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `oauth.choices-stricter-oauth` Choices stricter than OAuth: a `client_id` that is the URL of a client metadata document, authenticated with `private_key_jwt` and an assertion addressed to the issuer, with its `jwks_uri` and `redirect_uris` on the `client_id`'s domain (4.1); `revocation_endpoint` and `grant_types_supported`, including `refresh_token`, in the issuer's metadata (3.2); `iss` in every authorization response, and exact matching of `redirect_uri` as RFC 9700 requires (4.2); RFC 10027's best practices for Device Sign-In, and a check of the sign-in link's host (4.3); a refresh token from every sign-in (4.4); and `scope` on every sign-in request, with at least one scope granted and none beyond those requested (4.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L105) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `oauth.discovery-descriptions-poppy` Discovery and descriptions: `poppy.json`, including `auth.disabled` to offer no sign-in and `web.disabled` to ask Personal Agents not to browse, supported versions, described scopes, and scope hints (section 3, 4.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L106) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `oauth.sessions-session-header` Sessions: the Session header, which names the Personal Agent, the User, and the Session on every request, signed in or out, without an authorization-server grant (section 5) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L107) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `oauth.signed-delegated-personal` It is signed with a delegated key, which a key in the Personal Agent's `jwks_uri` vouches for in a delegation carried in the JWT's `poppy_dlg` header (5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L108) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `oauth.interactions-above-oauth` Interactions above OAuth: browser join, with its `poppy:browser-sign-in` scope (section 6), APIs (section 7), conversations (section 8), excluded tasks, skills, and feedback (section 9), and extensions (3.3), including Operations _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L109) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `oauth.extension-grant-mediated` An extension grant: the Mediated Sign-In extension adds a grant type at the token endpoint, as RFC 6749 §4.5 allows _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/04-oauth.md#L110) | MUST | both |  |

| ! | `bctl.website-scripts-keep` The website's own scripts keep running _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L48) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.user-ends-control` Only the User ends their control, by handing it back or cancelling _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L49) | MUST | both |  |

| → | `bctl.personal-agent-keep` The Personal Agent MUST NOT keep its own requests, or its conversation with the User, waiting until the User acts [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L51) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

| ! | `ucp.requests-follow-bindings` Requests follow UCP's Ask bindings and section 4 of this page, not spec 8.2–8.13 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L77) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `ucp.company-list-poppy` A Company MAY list a `poppy` entry too, for example a support agent run by another provider [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L78) | MAY | company |  |

| ! | `ucp.translation-small-caveats` The translation is small, and the two caveats below it are the whole of what doesn't carry over _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L81) | MUST | both |  |
