| ! | `ucp.conversation-company-chosen` \| Conversation, with a Company-chosen `conversation_id` \| `conversation.id`, Company-returned; replay it on follow-ups \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L83) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.conversation-lifetime-conversation` \| Conversation lifetime \| `conversation.expires_at`, Company-chosen \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L84) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.message-text-query` \| Message `text` \| `query` \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L85) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.message-data-resources` \| Message `data` \| `ids`: the resources the question is about \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L86) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.message-context-locale` \| Message `context` (`locale`, `time_zone`, `user_available`) \| `context` (`language`, `address_country`, `currency`, …); `locale` → `language` \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L87) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.request-idempotency-idempotency` \| Request `id`, as idempotency key \| UCP's idempotency key (`Idempotency-Key`, or `meta["idempotency-key"]` over MCP) \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L88) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-reply-message` \| The Company's reply, as `message` events with plain `text` \| `answer.plain` (`markdown`, `html` optional), plus `links` and `messages` \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L89) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.working-handoff-closed` \| `working`, `handoff`, `closed` \| `working` is `false` after every turn: Ask is synchronous. No handoff, and no close \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L90) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.responder-author-type` \| `responder`, `author.type` \| None. A `query` is the Personal Agent's words, `agent` by spec 8.8 \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L91) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.authorization-event-insufficient` \| `authorization` event (`insufficient_scope`, `scope`) \| 401 `identity_required` or 403 `insufficient_scope` on the request itself (4); or an `insufficient_scope` message in `messages` when the Company answered what it could \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L92) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.handoff-person-direct` \| Handoff to a person, Direct Conversation \| None \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L93) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.conversation-carries-context` `conversation.id` carries context, not authority: each turn is authorized by the credential it carries, as spec 8.11 also requires of this protocol's conversations _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L94) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.question-asks-action` A question that asks for an action gets an answer that says it wasn't performed, optionally with UCP's `operation_not_performed` message _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L95) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.whether-perform-through` Whether to perform it through the UCP capability that owns it is the Personal Agent's decision from the User's request, not the answer's _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L96) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5.1 User IDs and Agent IDs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `sessions.personal-agent-give` The Personal Agent MUST give each of its Users a User ID for each Company, using the Company's identifier (3.2) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L11) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `sessions.contain-derived-personal` It MUST NOT contain or be derived from personal information, such as an email address, phone number, or name, even with a keyed hash [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L12) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `sessions.personal-agent-instead` A Personal Agent MAY instead give a User a new User ID for each anonymous browsing session, like a private browser window [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L13) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.personal-agent-uses` The Personal Agent uses the ID for nothing else, discards it when the browsing session ends, and MUST NOT send an access token in a Session that uses it (5.4) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L14) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.personal-agent-acts` A Personal Agent that acts for a User through several agents, such as a travel agent and a shopping agent, MAY say which one a Session is for with an Agent ID [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L15) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `sessions.agent-follows-same` The Agent ID follows the same rules as the User ID: it is stable, opaque, different for each Company, and MUST NOT contain or be derived from personal information [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L16) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `sessions.agent-name-separate` An Agent ID doesn't name a separate party: the Personal Agent is still the client the Company deals with (4.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `sessions.company-agent-tell` The Company MAY use the Agent ID to tell a User's agents apart, but they share the User's account, refresh tokens, and conversations [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L18) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `sessions.personal-agent-holds` The Personal Agent holds the User IDs and Agent IDs of each of its Users at every Company, and MUST keep that mapping confidential: it MUST NOT publish it or share it with third parties, other than service providers that process it on the Personal Agent's behalf [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L19) | MUST | both |  |

## §5.2 The Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `session.personal-agent-send` The Personal Agent MUST send a `Poppy-Session` header on every request to a Company's APIs, conversations, and other resource endpoints this protocol or an extension defines [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.sharing-hostname-urls` Sharing a hostname with one of these URLs doesn't make another URL a Session destination _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L23) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-send-2` The Personal Agent MUST NOT send a Company's Session JWT to any other destination, except the website pages below [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L24) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.discovery-description-documents` Discovery and description documents and OAuth endpoints don't carry this header _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L25) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.poppy-session-mistaken` `typ` MUST be `poppy-session+jwt`, so the JWT can't be mistaken for a client assertion, delegation, or any other JWT (RFC 8725 §3.11) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L26) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.es256-every-personal` `alg` MUST be `ES256`, so every Personal Agent and Company can work together [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L27) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.signed-delegated-thumbprint` The JWT is signed with a delegated key, `kid` is that key's JWK thumbprint, and `poppy_dlg` carries its delegation (Delegated keys, below) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L28) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-client` `iss` is the Personal Agent's `client_id` (4.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L29) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.company-identifier-single` `aud` is the Company's identifier (3.2), as a single string (10.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L30) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.issuer-present-https` It is the issuer when present, or `https://{organization.domain}` with the host in lowercase and no trailing slash otherwise _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L31) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-choose` The Personal Agent MUST choose it at random, so it can't be guessed [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L32) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.other-session-companies` MUST NOT use it for any other Session, so Companies can't link Sessions by it [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L33) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.uses-same-characters` It uses the same characters as Conversation IDs (8.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.user-company` `sub` is the User ID for this Company (5.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L35) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.agent-optional-agent` `agent_id` is the optional Agent ID (5.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L36) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.request-method-without` `htm` and `htu` are the request's method and URL, without the query or fragment, as in a DPoP proof (RFC 9449 §4.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L37) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-signed` `iat` is when the Personal Agent signed it, in Unix seconds, and `jti` is unique and unguessable _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L38) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.hash-access-token` `ath` is the SHA-256 hash of the access token, base64url-encoded, when the request carries one, as in a DPoP proof _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L39) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-include` The Personal Agent MUST include every claim except `agent_id`, and `ath` when there's no access token [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L40) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.send-same-agent` It MUST send the same `sub` and `agent_id`, or no `agent_id`, in every Session JWT for a Session [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L41) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.session-replace-dpop` The Session JWT doesn't replace DPoP: it names the Session and User, which a DPoP proof doesn't, and it covers signed-out requests, which have no token for a DPoP proof to bind to _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L42) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.website-pages-personal` Website pages. A Personal Agent that fetches a page of the Company's website with its own HTTP client, rather than a browser, SHOULD send the Session header with it, so the Company can tell which Personal Agent and Session the request is from [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L43) | SHOULD | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-send-3` The Personal Agent MUST NOT send an access token with these requests, so the JWT has no `ath` and the request is signed out (5.4), even when a browser joined to the Session is signed in [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L44) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.headless-browser-browser` A headless browser is a browser: it joins the Session as section 6 describes, and doesn't send the header _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.page-redirects-personal` When a page redirects, the Personal Agent signs a new Session JWT for the new URL only if its host is still `organization.domain`, and otherwise follows the redirect without the header _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L46) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.personal-agent-fetch` The Personal Agent MAY then fetch the page again without the header [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L47) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.es256-ps384` `alg` is `ES256` or `PS384` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L48) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.companies-accept-delegations` Companies MUST accept delegations signed with `ES256` [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L49) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.accept-delegations-signed` SHOULD accept delegations signed with `PS384`. `PS384` lets a Personal Agent have its delegations signed blindly (10.7) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L50) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `session.poppy-delegation-delegation` `typ` MUST be `poppy-delegation+jwt`, so a delegation can't be used as a Session JWT [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L51) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.names-jwks-signed` `kid` names the key in `jwks_uri` that signed the delegation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L52) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-client-2` `iss` is the Personal Agent's `client_id` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.delegated-public-confirmation` `cnf.jwk` is the delegated public key, in the confirmation claim of RFC 7800 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L54) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.contain-private-members` It MUST NOT contain private key members [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L55) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `session.delegation-issued-expires` `iat` and `exp` are when the delegation was issued and when it expires. `exp` MUST be at most 24 hours after `iat` [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-chooses` The Personal Agent chooses the lifetime within that limit _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L57) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.unique-unguessable-delegation` `jti` is a unique, unguessable ID for the delegation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L58) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-user` The Personal Agent MUST NOT put a User ID, an Agent ID, a Company's issuer, or anything else about the User or the Companies they use in a delegation [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L59) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.poppy-delegation-compact` `poppy_dlg` is the delegation, in compact form _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L60) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.delegated-thumbprint-7638` `kid` is the delegated key's JWK thumbprint (RFC 7638) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L61) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-sign` The Personal Agent MUST NOT sign a Session JWT after its delegation's `exp` [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L62) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.verifying-session-header` When verifying a Session header (5.3), the Company MUST reject, with `invalid_session`, a Session JWT without a delegation, including one signed directly with a key from `jwks_uri`, and a Session JWT whose delegation fails any of these checks [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L63) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `session.resource-sees-many` A resource sees many Session JWTs with the same delegation, so it MAY cache a verified delegation until it expires [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L64) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `session.company-expect-user` So a Company MUST NOT expect a User's delegated key to stay the same between requests or Sessions, or treat a new one as a reason to reject a request [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L65) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-delegated` The Personal Agent MUST use each delegated key, and its delegation, for one User ID only: it signs with it only that User ID's Session JWTs [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L66) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `session.company-reject-invalid` A Company MAY reject, with `invalid_session`, a Session JWT whose delegated key has already signed for a different User ID while a delegation for the key lasts [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L67) | MAY | company |  |

## §5.3 Verifying the Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `session.companies-verify-session` Companies SHOULD verify the Session header on every request that carries it [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L70) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `session.company-complete-following` The Company MUST complete the following checks before relying on Session claims for client or User identity, ownership, continuity, or access to state, including creating or continuing a Session: [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L71) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.without-access-token` Without an access token, `ath` MUST be absent. 4 [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L72) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `session.endpoint-uses-session` An endpoint that uses no Session claims MAY handle a request without verifying the header or requiring one [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L73) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `session.company-unverified-session` The Company MUST NOT use unverified Session claims to attribute a request to a Personal Agent, User, or Session, or to look up their state [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L74) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `session.failed-session-check` A failed Session check returns HTTP 400 with `{"error": "invalid_session"}`, and an ended Session returns `{"error": "session_ended"}` (5.5) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L75) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `session.either-include-error` Either MAY include an `error_description` for the developer, as in RFC 6749 §5.2 [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L76) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `session.session-errors-rather` Session errors use 400 rather than 401 so that OAuth libraries, which treat a 401 as a problem with the access token, don't discard a valid token _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L77) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.company-reject-request` The Company MUST reject a request without the Session header when handling it depends on Session claims [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L78) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.personal-agent-still` The Personal Agent still sends the header on every request 5.2 requires, even when the Company doesn't verify it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L79) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `session.replayed-jwts-company` Replayed JWTs. A Company MAY reject a reused `jti`, as RFC 9449 §11.1 allows for DPoP proofs [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L80) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-sign-2` A Personal Agent SHOULD also sign requests carrying the Session header with an HTTP Message Signature (RFC 9421), using Web Bot Auth, so traffic-management infrastructure can authenticate the operator before the request reaches the Company's application [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L81) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.absence-make-session` Its absence does not make a Session JWT invalid _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L82) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.personal-agent-operator` The Personal Agent's operator signature MUST cover `poppy-session`, and `authorization` when present, so it binds to the Session JWT and access token [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L83) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.before-trusting-session` Before trusting any Session claim, the Company MUST verify the Session JWT independently (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L84) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.shared-origin-alone` A shared origin alone does not establish that two client metadata URLs name the same client _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L85) | MUST | both |  |

## §5.4 Signing in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `sessions.anonymous-no-sign-in` The Personal Agent MUST NOT send an access token in a Session that uses an anonymous browsing User ID (5.1) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L88) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `signin.sign-plain-oauth` Sign-in is plain OAuth, and doesn't need to know the Session _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L89) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `signin.company-reject-request` A Company MAY reject a request whose access token is for a different account than its Session used before, with `session_ended` (5.5) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L90) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `signin.personal-agent-start` A Personal Agent SHOULD start a new Session rather than use a second account in one Session, so accounts don't get mixed up across Sessions [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L91) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `signin.user-present` A Personal Agent MUST use Direct or Device Sign-In only when the User signs in themselves [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L92) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `signin.company-always-verify` A Company can't always verify this, for example if the Personal Agent completes a sign-in page itself, and MAY revoke a `client_id` that doesn't follow it (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L93) | MAY | both |  |

## §5.5 Ending Sessions and signing out

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `signout.company-remember-sessions` A Company MAY remember the `sid`s of Sessions it ended, for as long as it chooses, so an ended Session doesn't silently start again [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L96) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `signout.request-remembered-ended` A request for a remembered ended Session gets `session_ended` (HTTP 400, JSON body), and the Personal Agent MUST then start a new Session with a new `sid` and send the request again in it [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L97) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `signout.session-state-cart` The old Session's state, such as a cart or a browser's cookie, doesn't carry over _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L98) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `signout.personal-agent-finds` The Personal Agent finds out when a request fails with `invalid_token`, or refresh returns `invalid_grant`, and then continues signed out _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L99) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `signout.what-need-account` What doesn't need the account carries on, such as a cart or a conversation that hasn't used it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L100) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `signout.anything-used-account` Anything that used the account, such as a conversation (8.11) or an operation (Operations extension), stays as it is, but a request on it without an access token for that account gets a challenge (section 7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L101) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `signout.conversation-stays-open` A conversation stays open, so the User can sign in again and continue it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L102) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `signout.personal-agent-sign` The Personal Agent SHOULD NOT sign in to that account again unless the User asks [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L103) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5.6 Sending requests

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `requests.companies-accept-session` Companies MUST accept the Session header and access token at their APIs, conversations, and other protocol and extension endpoints without requiring cookies [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L106) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `requests.browser-website-carries` A browser on the website carries a cookie instead (section 6) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L107) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `requests.personal-agents-leave` Personal Agents MUST NOT leave out the Session header to appear to the Company as a person on their own, including on website pages they fetch without a browser, other than fetching a page again after `invalid_session` (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L108) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `requests.browser-follows-section` A browser follows section 6 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L109) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `requests.personal-agents-send` Personal Agents MUST NOT send tokens or Session JWTs in a URL [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L110) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `requests.companies-accept` Companies MUST NOT accept them from one [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L111) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `requests.rate-limits-company` Rate limits. A Company that limits how often a Personal Agent can make requests returns HTTP 429 (RFC 6585 §4) with a `Retry-After` header (RFC 9110 §10.2.3) when a request goes over the limit, on any of its endpoints, APIs, conversations, or website _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L112) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `requests.personal-agent-wait` The Personal Agent MUST wait at least that long before sending the request again [↗](pap-0.4/05-sessions.md#L113) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 Web browsing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `web.join-session-sends` It doesn't join a Session for that, and sends the Session header instead, always signed out (5.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L7) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `web.personal-agent-join` When it does, the Personal Agent MUST join its browser to a Session before browsing the Company's website [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L8) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.personal-agent-browser` A Personal Agent SHOULD NOT use a browser on the website of a Company that sets it, and uses the interfaces the Company lists instead. `web.disabled` doesn't cover pages the Personal Agent fetches without a browser (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L9) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `web.company-sets-disabled` A Company that sets `web.disabled` MUST NOT list `browser_session_endpoint` [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L10) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.list-agent-apis` MUST list `agent` or `apis` [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L11) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.says-what-company` It says what the Company prefers, and isn't a promise that Personal Agents won't browse _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L12) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `web.personal-agent-join-2` The Personal Agent MUST join only a browser it controls to a Session, never the User's own browser [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L13) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `web.form-hidden-field` The form has a hidden field named `code` with a one-time code, and posts to the endpoint _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L14) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.company-make-code` The Company MUST make the code unguessable and short-lived, and each code works once [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L15) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.company-code-browser` The Company MUST tie the code to the browser that loaded the page with a cookie set in the same response, so that only that browser can submit it [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L16) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.cookie-sent-form` The cookie MUST NOT be sent with a form submitted from another site [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L17) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `web.other-hosts-company` other hosts on the Company's domain MUST NOT be able to set it [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L18) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.otherwise-another-host` Otherwise another host could set its own cookie in a victim's browser and pair it with a code an attacker authorized _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L19) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.company-chooses-name` The Company chooses its name and value _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L20) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.page-stored-caches` The page MUST NOT be stored by caches, framed by other pages, or kept as a window reference by the page that opened it [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L21) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `web.loading-page-start` Loading the page MUST NOT start, end, or change any Session, or change the browser's other cookies [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L22) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `web.signing-needs-poppy` Signing in needs `poppy:browser-sign-in`. The Company MUST reject an access token in step 2 that doesn't have the `poppy:browser-sign-in` scope, with `insufficient_scope` as at an API (section 7) [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.company-lists-browser` A Company that lists `browser_session_endpoint` and offers sign-in MUST support `poppy:browser-sign-in` (4.7), though it MAY grant it to fewer clients or Users, as for any scope [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `web.personal-agent-take` The Personal Agent MUST take the code only from the page its own browser loaded from the endpoint in step 1 [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L25) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.authorize-code-anywhere` MUST NOT authorize a code from anywhere else, such as a message, a conversation, or another page [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L26) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `web.company-check` The Company MUST check that: [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L27) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.request-cookie-step` The request has the cookie from step 1, and it matches `code` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L28) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.code-authorized-step` The code was authorized in step 2, hasn't expired, and hasn't been submitted before _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L29) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.code-used-first` A code is used by the first request that submits it, whatever the result _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L30) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.sets-cookie-returns` If not, it sets no cookie and returns an error page with an error status _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L31) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.join-without-access` In a join without an access token, the Company SHOULD NOT end or change that login, because the Personal Agent's browser may have a login it can't easily recreate [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L32) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.scopes-apply-login` Scopes don't apply to that login, which the browser had without this protocol _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L33) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.join-access-token` A join with an access token signs the browser in to the account from step 2, with its scopes, in place of any login it had, and an earlier login doesn't come back: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.browser-before-join` \| Browser before \| Join \| While joined \| When the Session's sign-in ends \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L35) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.logged-without-access` \| Not logged in \| Without access token \| Not logged in. Requests belong to the Session \| Not logged in \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L36) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.logged-access-token` \| Not logged in \| With access token for A \| Signed in to A, with the token's scopes \| Signed out \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L37) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.logged-without-access-2` \| Logged in as A \| Without access token \| Still logged in as A through the browser's own login \| Logged in as A \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L38) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.logged-access-token-2` \| Logged in as A or B \| With access token for A \| Signed in to A, with the token's scopes \| Signed out \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L39) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.step` MUST be set only in step 3 [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L40) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.account-scopes-authorized` MUST act for the account and scopes authorized in step 2, if any [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L41) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.stop-acting-account` MUST stop acting for the account when the User signs out or disconnects the Personal Agent (5.5) [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L42) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `web.outlive-session` MUST NOT outlive the Session [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L43) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `web.what-poppy-browser` What `poppy:browser-sign-in` allows. After a signed-in join, the Company's website MUST either apply the cookie's scopes, as the Company's APIs apply an access token's, or treat `poppy:browser-sign-in` as access to everything the account can do on the website [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L44) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `web.website-applies-cookie` When the website applies the cookie's scopes, `poppy:browser-sign-in` allows nothing beyond the token's other scopes, and the Company MAY grant it without asking the User [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L45) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `web.poppy-browser-sign` When `poppy:browser-sign-in` gives the account's full access on the website, the Company MUST describe it that way (4.7), such as "Browse the website [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L46) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.anything-account-direct` see and do anything your account can do there," and in Direct and Device Sign-In MUST ask the User to approve it like any other scope [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L47) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.company-whose-website` A Company whose website treats `poppy:browser-sign-in` as the account's full access MUST set `web.unscoped` to `true` in `poppy.json`, so the Personal Agent knows what the scope allows before requesting it [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L48) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.company-sets-unscoped` A Company that sets `web.unscoped` MUST list `browser_session_endpoint` [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L49) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.website-refuses-action` When the website refuses an action because the Session lacks a scope, it SHOULD show a visible error message that names the missing scopes, so the Personal Agent can request them (5.4) [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L50) | SHOULD | both |  |
| → | `web.personal-agent-join-3` The Personal Agent MAY join again at any time, for example to sign the website in after signing in, to change its scopes, or when the website no longer recognizes the Session [↗](pap-0.4/06-web.md#L51) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 Who controls the browser

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `bctl.user-while-user` `"user"` while the User holds control (5) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L54) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `bctl.page-reads-needs` The page reads it when it needs it, such as when a marked button is pressed, and MAY send it to the Company with the request: [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L55) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.value-correct-guarantee` The value should be correct, but it isn't a guarantee (8.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `bctl.company-record-action` A Company MAY record it with the action, or use it to choose what its page does, such as showing "This step is for you to complete" when it reads `"agent"` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L57) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.rely-user-guarantee` It MUST NOT rely on `"user"` as a guarantee that the User took the step [↗](pap-0.4/ext-browser-control.md#L58) | MUST NOT | both |  |

## §6 Mediated Sign-In Security

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `mediated.personal-agents-send` Personal Agents MUST NOT send credentials anywhere other than the `token_endpoint` of the Company's issuer, with this grant [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L38) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.personal-agent-choose` A Personal Agent MUST choose which stored credentials to send by the Company's issuer, never by the field labels or the endpoint [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L39) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.show-company-organization` MUST show the Company's `organization.name` and domain whenever it asks the User for credentials or a code [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L40) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.once-refresh-token` Once it has a refresh token, the Personal Agent doesn't need the credentials to get access tokens _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L41) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.storing-credentials-after` Storing credentials. After a sign-in ends, with tokens or an error other than `code_required`, the Personal Agent MUST either discard the credentials or keep them only in a credential store the User chose, such as a password manager [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L42) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `mediated.keep-anywhere-else` It MUST NOT keep them anywhere else, including model context and logs (spec 10.2) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L43) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `mediated.after-user-company` After the User or the Company revokes the Personal Agent's access (spec 5.5), the Personal Agent SHOULD NOT sign in again with stored credentials unless the User asks it to [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L44) | SHOULD NOT | both |  |
| → | `signin.prefer-delegated` A Personal Agent SHOULD use Direct or Device Sign-In rather than Mediated Sign-In when the Company offers it and its scopes cover the task [↗](pap-0.4/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L45) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 UCP Commerce and approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.payment-payment-part` Payment. Payment is part of UCP checkout: the Company's UCP profile advertises the payment handlers it accepts, the Personal Agent's platform profile says which it supports, and the checkout carries the instrument _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L99) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-advertises-extension` For a Company that advertises this extension, UCP is its payment mechanism, and a Personal Agent that supports the extension pays through it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L100) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.approval-checkout-carries` Approval. UCP's checkout carries its own approval _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L101) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.checkout-resource-terms` The checkout resource is the terms; UCP's messages say when the User's review is required and when a step must finish on the Company's page (7); the User reviews and approves the checkout in a trusted interface, as UCP requires; and Complete Checkout is the call the Personal Agent makes once the User has committed _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L102) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.approval-purchase-company` That is the one approval for a purchase, so a Company SHOULD NOT also return an operation for a UCP capability's operation, unless a UCP extension the two have negotiated defines how an operation rides in a UCP response; two approval records for one action can disagree [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L103) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| → | `ucp.personal-agent-receives` A Personal Agent that receives one outside such an extension treats it as content (spec 10.1) and approves nothing _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L104) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.retries-idempotency-keys` Retries. UCP's idempotency keys and checkout lifecycle give a retried completion the first result _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L105) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.operations-extension-retry` The Operations extension's retry rules apply to the Company's other APIs _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L106) | MUST | company |  |

| → | `tokens.scheme` Signed in. The Personal Agent uses the token as its `token_type` names (4.5) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L12) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `apis.company-whose-server` A Company whose MCP server doesn't accept DPoP returns Bearer tokens for it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L13) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tokens.mcp-resource` The Personal Agent MUST request a token with `resource` set to the MCP server's `url` from `poppy.json`, as MCP authorization requires (4.5) [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L14) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `apis.resource-server-protected` The `resource` in the server's protected resource metadata MUST equal that `url` [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L15) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.token-works-server` Each such token works only at the MCP server whose `url` equals its `resource`, including when other endpoints share its host _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L16) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.company-reject-elsewhere` The Company MUST reject it elsewhere [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L17) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `apis.signed-server-accepts` Signed out. An MCP server that accepts the Session header can take signed-out calls with the Session header only, if it allows them _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L18) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.without-session-verification` Without Session verification. An MCP server that ignores the Session header can identify the client and account through a validated access token, or serve signed-out requests that use no Session claims _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L19) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.calls-join-session` Its calls don't join the Session's cart, conversations, or website _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L20) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.company-wants-connections` A Company that wants those connections has the server verify the Session header (5.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L21) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `apis.other-clients-offers` Other MCP clients. When it offers account access, the server's protected resource metadata tells MCP clients where to get a token _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L22) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.names-company-issuer` It names the Company's issuer, not the Personal Agent: an MCP server that offers account access MUST include the Company's issuer in its `authorization_servers` [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L23) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.clients-implement-protocol` MCP clients that don't implement this protocol sign in with MCP's own authorization flow, outside this protocol, and their requests belong to no Session _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L24) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `apis.error-code-request` \| No error code \| 401 \| The request needs the User's account, and has no access token. The challenge's `scope` attribute names the scopes needed, as RFC 6750 §3.1 describes. The Personal Agent handles it as `insufficient_scope`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L25) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `apis.invalid-token-access` \| `invalid_token` \| 401 \| The access token is expired, revoked, or invalid. The Personal Agent refreshes it (4.4), or continues signed out if refresh fails (5.5). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L26) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `apis.insufficient-scope-access` \| `insufficient_scope` \| 403 \| The access token lacks the scopes the request needs, which the response names in the `scope` attribute. The Personal Agent uses a refresh token that covers them (4.4), or signs in (5.4), and retries, unless the User signed out or disconnected it (5.5). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L27) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `apis.invalid-session-json` \| `invalid_session` \| 400 \| In a JSON body. A required Session header is missing or Session verification fails (5.3), or the Company refuses the `client_id` (4.1). A new Session doesn't fix it: the Personal Agent stops sending the request until it fixes the cause, such as an expired delegation or a wrong `htu`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L28) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.session-ended-json` \| `session_ended` \| 400 \| In a JSON body. The Session has ended, or the Company refuses an account change in it (5.4, 5.5). The Personal Agent starts a new Session and sends the request again, once. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L29) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `apis.version-unsupported-json` \| `version_unsupported` \| 400 \| In a JSON body. `Poppy-Version` is missing, or the Company doesn't serve a compatible version (3.4). The Personal Agent fetches `poppy.json` again, and if it chooses another version, starts a new Session and sends the request again, once. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L30) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `apis.extension-required-json` \| `extension_required` \| 403 \| In a JSON body. The request needs an extension it doesn't declare, named in `extension` (3.3). An MCP server returns it only to refuse the Personal Agent entirely, not for one tool. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L31) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `apis.unverified-header-establish` An unverified header does not establish either identity _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/07-apis.md#L32) | MUST | both |  |

## §8 UCP Sessions and UCP resources

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ucp.workflow-outlive-session` A workflow can outlive the Session that created it: the Personal Agent MAY continue it in a later Session for the same User while the workflow remains available and the Company's access policy allows [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L112) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.reuse-user-workflow` It MUST NOT reuse one User's UCP workflow identifier for another User [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L113) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `ucp.personal-agent-sends` The Personal Agent sends the Session header on its UCP requests as on any API (spec 5.2), with the same `sid` for every request in a task _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L114) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `ucp.company-verify-header` A Company MAY verify the header at its UCP endpoints (4) and group the UCP workflows a Session creates under that Session, so they appear on the website after a browser join and the User is recognized across Sessions by User ID (spec 5.1) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L115) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `ucp.grouping-changes-nothing` Grouping changes nothing about the workflows themselves, and this extension doesn't expect it: a Personal Agent MUST NOT assume that a cart or checkout it created through UCP appears on the Company's website, in a Company Agent conversation, or in another Session unless the Company says so [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L116) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `ucp.endpoint-instead-ignore` A UCP endpoint MAY instead ignore the Session header, as spec 7 allows an MCP server to [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L117) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.unlike-server-still` Unlike such a server, it still takes signed-out calls from Personal Agents: UCP identifies the Personal Agent on every request by its platform profile and operator signature (4), so the Company knows which Personal Agent is calling without the header _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L118) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.company-choice` Which of the two is the Company's choice _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L119) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ucp.company-require-verified` A Company MAY also require a verified Session header on requests through this extension, and rely on its claims (4) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L120) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.used-independently-follows` UCP used independently follows section 2 and the Company's UCP access policy _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L121) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.request-without-user` A UCP request without a user token is signed out, and one with a user token is signed in to that token's account, whatever the Session's history _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L122) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.workflow-follows-access` Each UCP workflow follows its own access policy across that change, as UCP defines; this protocol's rules for its own conversations after sign-out (spec 5.5) don't carry over to UCP workflows _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L123) | MUST | both |  |

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.message-company-sets` \| `id` \| No \| The message's ID. The Company sets it when it records the message as an event (8.5): the request's ID for the Personal Agent's messages (8.3), or an ID it chooses for its own. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L39) | MAY | both |  |

| – | `conversations.request-message-company` \| `as_of_request` \| No \| On a message from the Company Agent, the ID of the latest request it took into account (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L41) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.cursor-message-personal` \| `as_of_cursor` \| No \| On a message the Personal Agent wrote, the last cursor it had read (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L42) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.author-wrote-message` \| `author` \| Yes \| Who wrote the message. `type` is `agent` if the Personal Agent wrote it, `human` if the User wrote it (8.8). Company messages can also name the writer (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L43) | MUST | both |  |

| – | `conversations.data-json-object` \| `data` \| No \| A JSON object for structured details that would need markup, like a list or a table, to fit in a sentence. The protocol doesn't define its keys. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L45) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `conversations.context-facts-user` \| `context` \| No \| Facts about the User's situation, such as `locale`, `time_zone`, and `user_available` (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L46) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `conversations.extensions-content-defined` \| `extensions` \| No \| Content defined by extensions, keyed by extension name (below). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L47) | MAY | both |  |

| ✓ | `conv.message-content` A message MUST have at least one of `text`, `data`, `context`, or `extensions` [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L49) | MUST | both | `conv/message-content` |
| ! | `conversations.person-types-while` A person types while messages arrive, so which messages they had read when they sent one isn't known _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L50) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `conversations.request-message-company-2` `as_of_request`: a message from the Company Agent, with `author.type` `agent`, MAY include the ID of the latest message, handoff request, or handoff cancel from the Personal Agent that it took into account [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L51) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.because-company-acts` Because the Company acts on requests in the order it accepts them (8.3), it also took into account every request accepted before that one _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L52) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-tell` A Personal Agent can use it to tell whether a reply covers its latest message without waiting for `working` to be `false` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.taking-request-account` Taking a request into account doesn't mean the Company acted on it, because a close can drop requests (8.12) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L54) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `conversations.cursor-message-personal-2` `as_of_cursor`: a message the Personal Agent wrote, with `author.type` `agent`, MAY include the cursor of the last read it had handled when it wrote the message (8.5), if it has one [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L55) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.company-tell-messages` The Company can then tell which of its messages the Personal Agent had seen _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.message-person-company` A message from a person at the Company, or written by the User, with `author.type` `human`, MUST NOT include either field [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L57) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-personal-agent` The Company and the Personal Agent MUST NOT depend on either field being present, and treat each only as a hint for interpreting the message [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L58) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.context-context-holds` Context. `context` holds facts about the User's situation that affect how the Company replies, so the Personal Agent doesn't have to write them into the text _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L59) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-shares` When a Personal Agent shares one of these facts, it MUST use the field and format defined here: [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.locale-language-5646` `locale` is a language tag such as `en-US` (RFC 5646), for the language and formatting of replies _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L61) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.time-zone-iana` `time_zone` is an IANA time zone name such as `America/Los_Angeles`, for reading and showing times _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L62) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.user-available-true` `user_available` is `true` if the User can answer questions right now _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L63) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `conversations.context-include-other` `context` MAY include other fields, such as accessibility needs or preferred units [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L64) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `conversations.company-agent-interprets` The Company Agent interprets them as it sees fit, and a Company MAY ignore them [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L65) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.type-required-agent` `type` is required: `agent` or `human`, as 8.8 describes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L66) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.stable-author-chosen` `id` is a stable ID for the author, chosen by the Company, so the Personal Agent can tell the same author's messages apart from others' _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L67) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.name-author-display` `name` is the author's display name, such as `Alex` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L68) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.image-author-picture` `image` is the URL of the author's picture, for the Personal Agent to show next to the name _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L69) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `conversations.company-whose-messages` A Company whose messages come from several people or AI personas MAY use them to say which one wrote each message [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L70) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.side-send-extension` A side MUST NOT send an extension's content unless the other side uses that extension with the same version: the Company checks the request's `Poppy-Extensions` (3.4), and the Personal Agent checks the Company's document for the version it chose (3.1) [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L71) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.like-other-fields` Like other fields, extension content the receiver doesn't support is ignored (3.3), so `text` and `data` carry what the message says _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L72) | MUST | both |  |

| ! | `conversations.message-message-message` \| `message` \| `message`: a message from either side, as it was sent, with `role` set by the Company to `user` or `company` for the side it came from. Every message the Company accepts is recorded, including one with only `context`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L75) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.state-handoff-responder` \| `state` \| `handoff`, `responder`, and `closed`, after any of them changes. See 8.7 for their values. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L76) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.authorization-error-scope` \| `authorization` \| `error` and `scope`: the Company needs sign-in or more scopes (8.11). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L77) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.user-requested-reason` \| `user_requested` \| `reason`: the Company asks to talk with the User directly (8.10). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L78) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-opened-direct` \| `direct_opened`, `direct_closed` \| `conversation_id`: a Direct Conversation linked to this one opened or closed (8.10). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L79) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conv.skip-unknown-events` Personal Agents MUST skip event types they don't recognize, so later versions and extensions can add types [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L80) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.cursor-wait-query` `cursor` and `wait` are query parameters, here and on the `POST` requests in 8.3 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L81) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.event-cursor` Each event's `id` is also a cursor _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L82) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.without-cursor-read` Without a `cursor`, the read starts at the beginning of the conversation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L83) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conv.cursor-opaque` Cursors are opaque, so the Personal Agent MUST NOT compare or sort them [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L84) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.wait-whole-number` `wait` is a whole number of seconds, 0 or more _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L85) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-holds-request` The Company holds the request for up to `wait` seconds until there is an event to return, or until `working` changes from `true` to `false` (8.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L86) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.return-sooner-wait` It MAY return sooner, or cap `wait`: a larger `wait` is held only as long as the cap, not rejected [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L87) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.without-wait-returns` Without `wait`, it returns right away _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L88) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.read-times-returns` A read that times out returns an empty `events` list _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L89) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.every-successful-read` Every successful read MUST include `conversation_id`, `events`, `cursor`, `has_more`, and the state fields `working`, `handoff`, `responder`, and `closed` (8.7), with `events` empty when there are none. `cursor` is the last event returned, or the request's cursor if there were none [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L90) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.more-true-personal` When `has_more` is `true`, the Personal Agent reads again right away _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L91) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.state-fields-state` The state fields are the state when the Company responds, so while `has_more` is `true` they can be newer than the events returned _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L92) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-applies` The Personal Agent applies events in order, and relies on the state fields once `has_more` is `false` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L93) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-handles` The Personal Agent handles events in order and saves the cursor after them _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L94) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.read-after-reconnect` A read after a reconnect can return events again, so it skips event IDs it has already handled _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L95) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-keeps-events` The Company keeps events for as long as it chooses _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L96) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.cursor-events-longer` A cursor for events it no longer has returns `cursor_expired` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L97) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-reads` The Personal Agent then reads from the beginning _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L98) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.6 Streaming

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.company-stream-events` A Company MAY stream events with server-sent events (SSE) [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L101) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-stream-returns` A Company that doesn't stream returns JSON as usual _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L102) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.changes-handoff-responder` Changes to `handoff`, `responder`, and `closed` arrive as `state` events. `working` isn't an event: the Company sends it as a `working` event with no SSE `id`, when the stream opens and each time it changes: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L103) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.company-close-stream` The Company MAY close a stream at any time, for example when the access token expires [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L104) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `conv.text-delta` While the Company Agent writes a message, the Company MAY send pieces of its text as `text-delta` events, with no SSE `id`: [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L105) | MAY | company |  |

## §8.7 State

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.working-true-false` \| `working` \| `true` or `false` \| The Company has work in progress: a request it accepted but hasn't acted on (8.3), a reply being written, or work it started on its own. Read again until it's `false`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L108) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.handoff-none-pending` \| `handoff` \| `none` or `pending` \| `pending` while the Company is looking for a person to join (8.9). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L109) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.responder-agent-human` \| `responder` \| `agent` or `human` \| Who is handling the Company side: an automated Company Agent, or a live person at the Company. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L110) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.closed-true-false` \| `closed` \| `true` or `false` \| The conversation takes no more messages (8.12). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L111) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-treats` A Personal Agent treats a `handoff` it doesn't recognize as `pending`, and a `responder` it doesn't recognize as `human` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L112) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.company-message-include` Each Company message MUST also include `author.type`, with `agent` or `human`, to identify who wrote it [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L113) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.8 Human or AI

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.agent-sender` On the Personal Agent's side, the Personal Agent MUST set each message's `author.type`: `agent` when the Personal Agent wrote it, and `human` only when it carries the User's own words [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L116) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.9 Handoff to a person

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.stop-looking-person` It MAY stop looking for a person, and `handoff` then becomes `none` [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L119) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `conversations.keep-looking-example` It MAY also keep looking, for example when its help desk can't withdraw a request already routed to someone [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L120) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-learns` The Personal Agent learns which happened from `handoff` and `responder`, and MUST NOT depend on the cancel taking effect [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L121) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.cancel-handoff-pending` A cancel when `handoff` isn't `pending` changes nothing _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L122) | MUST | both |  |

## §8.10 Direct Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.company-send-information` The Company MUST NOT send information there that it cannot share with the Personal Agent [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L125) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-returns-conversation-2` The Company returns a new Conversation ID as usual: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L126) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.parent-conversation-open` The parent conversation MUST be open, belong to the same owner (8.2), and not be a Direct Conversation itself [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L127) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.otherwise-company-returns` Otherwise the Company returns `conversation_not_found` for an unknown parent or one with a different owner, `conversation_closed` for a closed one, `invalid_request` for one that is a Direct Conversation, and `direct_conversation_open` for one that already has an open Direct Conversation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L128) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.event-change-conversation` The event doesn't change the conversation's state (8.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L129) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.company-reject-user` The Company MUST reject a `user_requested_event_id` that doesn't name a `user_requested` event in that parent with `invalid_request` [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L130) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.request-without-message` A request without `message` is valid only when starting a Direct Conversation with both IDs _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L131) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.repeating-same-parent` Repeating the same parent ID and event ID returns the same Direct Conversation without adding another message, even after it closes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L132) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.user-declines-available` If the User declines or isn't available, the Personal Agent says so in the parent conversation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L133) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.11 Sign-in during a conversation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.response-carrying-authorization` When a response carrying an `authorization` event has not yet sent its headers, the Company MAY also include the matching `WWW-Authenticate` challenge on the successful response, as RFC 9110 §11.6.1 allows [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L136) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.personal-agent-handle` The Personal Agent MUST handle the event and matching challenge as one authorization need [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L137) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conversations.resubmit-accepted-message` MUST NOT resubmit an accepted message because it received the challenge [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L138) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.conversation-tied-access` A conversation isn't tied to one access token or Session _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L139) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conv.token-switch` The Personal Agent MAY start or stop sending an access token partway through a conversation, after signing in, refreshing, or signing out, or continue it in a new Session, as long as the request matches the conversation's owner (8.2) [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L140) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.sending-message-authorize` Sending a message does not authorize the requested account action _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L141) | MUST | both |  |

## §8.12 Closing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.company-request-hasn` The Company MAY act on any request it hasn't acted on yet, or MAY drop it, whether it accepted the request before or after the close [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L144) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.happens-depend-timing` Which one happens can depend on timing, so the Personal Agent MUST NOT depend on either [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L145) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.close-sent-conversation` A close sent to a conversation that is already closed returns HTTP 202 and changes nothing _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L146) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.closing-conversation-cancel` Closing a conversation doesn't cancel anything it started, such as an order or a return _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L147) | MUST | both |  |

## §8.13 Errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conversations.conversation-found-conversation` \| `conversation_not_found` \| 404 \| The Conversation ID is unknown or belongs to a different Personal Agent, User, or account (8.2). All return the same error. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L150) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.conversation-closed-message` \| `conversation_closed` \| 409 \| A message, handoff request, or handoff cancel was sent to a closed conversation (8.12). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L151) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-conversation-open` \| `direct_conversation_open` \| 409 \| The conversation has an open Direct Conversation, named in `conversation_id` (8.10). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L152) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.request-conflict-request` \| `request_id_conflict` \| 409 \| A request reused an ID that the Company accepted with a different path or body (8.3). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L153) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.invalid-cursor-cursor` \| `invalid_cursor` \| 400 \| The cursor is unknown or doesn't belong to this conversation. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L154) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.cursor-expired-company` \| `cursor_expired` \| 410 \| The Company no longer has the events at this cursor (8.5). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L155) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.invalid-request-request` \| `invalid_request` \| 400 \| The request is malformed, such as a missing request `id` (8.3), a message with no content (8.4), an ID with characters not allowed (8.2), or a `wait` that isn't a whole number of seconds. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L156) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.extension-required-request` \| `extension_required` \| 403 \| The request needs an extension it doesn't declare, named in `extension` (3.3). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L157) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.version-mismatch-conversation` \| `version_mismatch` \| 409 \| The conversation started in other versions, and the Company doesn't continue it in these. The protocol version it started in is in `protocol_version` (8.2). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/08-conversations.md#L158) | MUST | company |  |

## §9 Task coverage

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `tasks.personal-agent-spend` A Personal Agent can spend a long time looking for a way to do a task that the Company doesn't offer through this protocol, and the Company sees only a customer who left _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L7) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.company-already-returns` A Company already returns errors in its responses (sections 7 and 8), including for a task it doesn't offer, and can see them in its own logs _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L8) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `tasks.excluded-tasks-tasks` \| `excluded_tasks` \| No \| The tasks the Company chose not to offer through this protocol (9.1). Defaults to none. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L9) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `tasks.skill-index-agent` \| `skill_index` \| No \| An Agent Skills discovery index of the skills the Company publishes (9.4). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L10) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `tasks.feedback-endpoint-https` \| `feedback` \| No \| `endpoint` is an HTTPS URL where Personal Agents report a User's task that can't be done (9.3). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L11) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.response-describes-what` The response describes what the Company offers, not the User's account, so the request carries no access token, even in a signed-in Session _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L12) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `tasks.company-give-different` A Company MAY give different Sessions different responses, based on the Session, User ID, or Agent ID, for example to try a new skill with some Users [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L13) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.verifies-session-header` It verifies the Session header before it does (5.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L14) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.company-gives-every` A Company that gives every Session the same response can serve it without verifying the header _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L15) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.company-gives-different` A Company that gives different Sessions different responses MUST mark them `private` or `no-store` in `Cache-Control` (RFC 9111 §5.2.2), so that a shared cache doesn't give one Session's response to another [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L16) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.personal-agent-response` A Personal Agent SHOULD get the response before it starts on a task in a Session [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L17) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `tasks.reuse-rest-session` It MAY reuse it for the rest of the Session, as its caching headers allow [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L18) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.another-session` MUST NOT use it in another Session [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L19) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.session-errors-invalid` Session errors are `invalid_session` and `session_ended` (5.3), and version errors `version_unsupported` (3.4) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L20) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.gets-response-personal` When it gets no response, the Personal Agent carries on as if the Company listed no excluded tasks, published no skills, and took no feedback _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L21) | MUST | both |  |

| ! | `tasks.page-user-open` \| `web` \| `url` \| A page the User can open on any HTTPS website, or in an app through an HTTPS link the app claims, such as an iOS universal link or an Android App Link. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L38) | MUST | both |  |

| ! | `tasks.website-browsing-uses` Website browsing uses cookies as in section 6 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L42) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.acting-another-company` Acting at another Company uses that Company's discovery, Session, and any needed account authorization _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L43) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.personal-agents-skip` Personal Agents MUST skip reference types they don't recognize, so later versions can add types, such as the Company Agent or an extension [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L44) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.alternative-content-company` An alternative is content from the Company (10.1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L45) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.instructions-describe-another` Its `instructions` describe another way to do the task on the User's behalf _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L46) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tasks.instructions-personal-agent` They are not instructions the Personal Agent has to follow _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L47) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9.3 Feedback

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tasks.user-task-done` When a User's task can't be done, the Personal Agent MAY send `POST {feedback.endpoint}` with the Session header (5.2), and a JSON body: [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L50) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.task-what-user` \| `task` \| Yes \| What the User was trying to do, in a short phrase, such as "Return a jacket", "Move a flight to the next day", or "Pay with a gift card". At most 200 characters. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L51) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tasks.description-what-personal` \| `description` \| Yes \| What the Personal Agent was trying to accomplish, in detail, and why, without identifiers such as order numbers, account numbers, or names. At most 2,000 characters. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L52) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.company-verify-session` A Company SHOULD verify the Session header on a report, signed in or signed out, and needs no scope for it [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L53) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.company-verify-header` The Company MUST verify the header before attributing a report to a Personal Agent, User, or Session [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L54) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.otherwise-accept-report` Otherwise it can accept the report without attribution (5.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L55) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.report-repeat-identities` The report doesn't repeat these identities or say where the problem happened _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `feedback.no-personal-data` Personal Agents SHOULD NOT put personal data in a report, such as the User's name, contact details, or order details [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L57) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.report-describes-task` A report describes the task, not the User _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L58) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `feedback.no-secrets` Personal Agents MUST NOT put secrets in a report (10.2) [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L59) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.once` A Personal Agent SHOULD send one report for each task it couldn't do, not one for each attempt [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L60) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.not-excluded` A Personal Agent SHOULD NOT report a task the Company lists as excluded (9.1), since the Company already knows it doesn't offer it [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L61) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.report-wrong-written` A report can be wrong, or written to mislead _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L62) | MUST | both |  |
| ✎ | `feedback.as-data` Companies MUST treat a report's text as data, not as instructions, including when a model reads it [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L63) | MUST | company | _reports go to the Company's feedback handler as data and never to a model; the FeedbackReport docs say so_ |
| – | `tasks.task-done-after` When the task can be done after all, it MAY instead respond with HTTP 200 and an alternative (9.2) as the body, such as the one in 9.2 for paying with a gift card [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L64) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `feedback.accept-either` Personal Agents MUST accept either response [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L65) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9.4 Agent context

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `tasks.company-include-skill` A Company MAY include `skill_index` in its tasks response (section 9) to publish skills for Personal Agents acting on the User's behalf at that Company [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L68) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.companies-publish-skill` Companies that publish `skill_index` MUST follow that revision's index format, artifact distribution, integrity, and HTTP requirements for artifacts, with the index in the tasks response instead of fetched from its own URL [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L69) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.personal-agents-index` Personal Agents that use the index MUST follow its verification and archive safety requirements before using a skill [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L70) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.personal-agents-ignore-2` Personal Agents MAY ignore `skill_index` and use those channels directly; a Company does not need to publish skills to support Poppy [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L71) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.urls-personal-agents` URLs. Personal Agents MUST resolve an entry's `url` against `tasks.endpoint`, using RFC 3986 §5 [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L72) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.listing-artifact-another` Listing an artifact on another domain does not make that domain an API endpoint or authorize sending it credentials or Session headers _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L73) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tasks.compatibility-personal-agents` Compatibility. Personal Agents SHOULD ignore unknown index fields [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L74) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skip-entries-unknown` SHOULD skip entries with an unknown `type` [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L75) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
