| → | `tasks.personal-agents-ignore-3` Personal Agents SHOULD ignore the index when `$schema` is absent or unknown; the rest of the tasks response remains usable [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L76) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `tasks.company-publish-same` A Company MAY also publish the same index at `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` for other clients [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L77) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.poppy-require-separate` Poppy does not require that separate index or require other skill clients to discover `poppy.json` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L78) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `tasks.personal-agents-descriptions` Personal Agents MAY use its descriptions and workflows to carry out the User's task [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L79) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.authorize-another-task` It does not authorize another task or override the Personal Agent's policies _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L80) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.personal-agents-execute` Personal Agents MUST NOT execute scripts from a skill unless the User or the Personal Agent's configuration explicitly allows it [↗](pap-0.4/09-tasks.md#L81) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10 UCP Security considerations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ucp.issuer-document-through` One issuer, one document. Through this extension, the Personal Agent uses the issuer it selected from the protected resource metadata at `organization.domain` (2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L129) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.signs-issuer-whatever` It signs in only at that issuer, whatever `realm` or `resource_metadata` a UCP challenge carries, so a UCP endpoint can't send the User to someone else's sign-in and a `poppy.json` can't send a User's token to someone else's UCP _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L130) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.what-domain-vouches` What the domain vouches for. The UCP profile is on the same host as `poppy.json` and can't redirect elsewhere (3), so whoever speaks for the Company in this protocol speaks for it in UCP (spec 10.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L131) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.authority-binding-shows` UCP's authority binding shows who published each schema the profile names, not that the Company should be trusted _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L132) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.content-company-product` Content from the Company. Product data, `messages`, and Ask answers are content from the Company (spec 10.1): data, never instructions, and never the User's approval of a purchase _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L133) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.answer-indicative-capability` An Ask answer is indicative; the capability that owns a resource is authoritative when they differ _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L134) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.messages-including-disclosures` UCP's own messages, including the disclosures UCP requires the Personal Agent to show, keep UCP's rules; the Disclosures extension covers this protocol's conversation messages, not UCP's _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L135) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.link-never-instruction` A link is never an instruction to act _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L136) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.scopes-travel-token` Scopes travel with the token, not the conversation. Replaying an Ask `conversation` carries no access from an earlier turn _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L137) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.turn-authorized-requires` Each turn is authorized on its own, as UCP requires and as spec 8.11 requires for this protocol's conversations _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L138) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.profiles-aren-user` Profiles aren't per User. A platform profile specific to a User would let Companies match that User across Companies by its URL, which User IDs prevent (spec 5.1) (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L139) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `ucp.payments-handles-payment` Payments. UCP handles payment through payment handlers the two profiles negotiate, which tokenize instruments so the Personal Agent carries tokens rather than raw credentials _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L140) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.tokens-credential-personal` Those tokens, and any credential the Personal Agent does handle, are secrets, kept out of model context with the others in spec 10.2 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L141) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.webhooks-platform-profile` Webhooks. A UCP platform profile can name a webhook URL for order updates _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L142) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ucp.webhooks-reach-personal` Webhooks reach the Personal Agent's own systems, which then learn which Companies its Users buy from, even when the rest of the Personal Agent keeps that on the User's device (spec 10.7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L143) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ucp.personal-agent-keeps` A Personal Agent that keeps that private leaves order webhooks out of its profile; one that uses them verifies their signatures as UCP requires _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-ucp.md#L144) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.1 Content from Companies

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.personal-agent-passes` A Personal Agent passes what a Company returns to its model: conversation messages, API descriptions and responses, MCP tool descriptions and results, web pages, skill indexes and skill contents (9.4), excluded tasks and alternatives (section 9) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L7) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `security.personal-agents-treat` Personal Agents MUST treat content from a Company as data, not as instructions [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L8) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.user-decides-what` Only the User decides what the Personal Agent does _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L9) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.no-cross-company` A Personal Agent MUST NOT act at one Company, or send it information, because content from another Company asked it to [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L10) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.acts-company-user` It acts at a Company only when the User's task needs it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L11) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `security.relevant-only` A Personal Agent SHOULD send a Company only information relevant to the User's task [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L12) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.includes-context-helps` That includes context that helps the Company handle it, such as the reason for a return or a deadline the User has _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L13) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `security.include-unrelated-details` It doesn't include unrelated details from the User's context or from other Companies _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L14) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `security.text-company-never` Text from a Company is never the User's approval or consent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L15) | MUST | company |  |

## §10.2 Secrets and the model

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.secrets-out-of-model` Following draft-ietf-wimse-aims §8, which keeps an agent's credentials out of the model's reach, Personal Agents MUST keep these out of model context: access tokens (4.5), refresh tokens (4.4), Session JWTs (5.2), private keys, authorization codes and PKCE code verifiers (4.2), and device codes (4.3) [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L18) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.other-secrets` Personal Agents SHOULD keep every other secret out of model context too, such as one-time codes, and sign and send requests in code the model can't read [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L19) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.3 What a domain vouches for

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.make-issuer-metadata` They don't make the issuer metadata more trustworthy than the domain, because the domain chooses the issuer _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L22) | MUST | both |  |

## §10.5 Signing in with the User's credentials

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.company-offers-direct` A Company that offers no Direct or Device Sign-In, or whose scopes and APIs don't cover what Users need, can expect Personal Agents to sign in that way, as the guides point out _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L25) | MUST | both |  |

## §10.6 Joining a browser to a Session

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.code-come-back` The code has to come back with the cookie set alongside it, so a code the attacker authorized in its own browser fails in the victim's, which doesn't have that cookie _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L28) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `security.browser-send-cookie` The browser doesn't send that cookie with a form submitted from another site, and other hosts on the Company's domain can't set it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L29) | MUST | company |  |

## §10.7 Delegated keys

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.keep-personal-agent` They keep a Personal Agent's own systems from learning which Companies a User works with only if those systems never see the delegated keys or the requests they sign, for example when delegated keys stay on the User's device _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L32) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `security.blind-signing-personal` Blind signing. A Personal Agent SHOULD have the keys in its `jwks_uri` sign client assertions and delegations blindly, unless its own systems need to see which Companies a User works with [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L33) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.variants-9474-recommends` The variants RFC 9474 recommends add a random prefix to the message, so their signatures don't verify as a JWT's _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `security.deterministic-variant-adds` The PSS-Deterministic variant adds nothing, so it is safe only when the message has a value the signer can't guess (RFC 9474 §7.3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L35) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `security.client-assertion-delegation` The `jti` of a client assertion or delegation is that value, so the Personal Agent MUST generate it on the User's device [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L36) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.personal-agent-signs` A Personal Agent that signs blindly MUST therefore sign both its client assertions and its delegations blindly [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L37) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.rely-signature-jwks` MUST NOT rely on a signature by a key in its `jwks_uri` to mean its own systems approved what it signed, for example to limit delegation lifetimes or to stop a User [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L38) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.8 Sign-ins someone else started

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.personal-agent-receives` A Personal Agent that receives the redirect only on the device that opened the authorization URL ties the tokens to that device, so a forwarded link fails (4.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L41) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.tell-users-browser` One that can tell which of its Users is in the browser at `redirect_uri`, such as by its own sign-in there, can check that it's the User who started the request _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L42) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `security.neither-possible-every` Neither is possible for every Personal Agent, such as one whose link opens in a new browser on another device _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L43) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.company-sign-consent` The Company's sign-in and consent pages name the Personal Agent that wants to connect, and tell the User to continue only if they just asked it to (guides) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L44) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `security.person-personal-agent` A person who doesn't use that Personal Agent, or didn't ask, can decline _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L45) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.help-person-tricked` This doesn't help when the person tricked uses the same Personal Agent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L46) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `security.both-sign-types` Both sign-in types follow the best practices in RFC 10027 §2 (4.2, 4.3), such as short-lived requests and limited scopes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/10-security.md#L47) | MUST | both |  |

## Operations 1 Introduction

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.perform-confirmed-only` Approval covers the exact terms. An approval covers one revision of the terms, and the Company performs only what that revision describes _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L7) | MUST | company | `ops/performs` |
| ! | `ops.most-once-retry` At most once. A retry with the same approval never performs the action twice (7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L8) | MUST | both |  |

## Operations 2 Advertising support

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.list-browser-session` It MUST list `web.browser_session_endpoint` with it (spec 6), because only a browser joined to a Session gets operations [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L11) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-returns-operations` A Company that returns no operations on its website doesn't list `endpoint` and doesn't serve it, and its website handles approval itself _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L12) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.extension-used-company` The extension is used only when the Company lists `operations` with `version` `"3"` and the request declares that version _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L13) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.company-return-operations` A Company MUST NOT return operations in response to a request that doesn't declare it [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L14) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `ops.server-returns-error` An MCP server returns that error only to refuse the Personal Agent entirely _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L15) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.tool-needs-extension` A tool that needs the extension returns an ordinary tool error instead (spec 7) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L16) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.different-major-version` A different major version doesn't count as support for this version _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |

## Operations 3 The operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.operation-identifies-action` \| `operation_id` \| Yes \| Identifies the action, not a kind of action _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L20) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.stays-same-terms` It stays the same when the terms change (see "New terms"), and the Company MUST NOT use it for another action [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L21) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.same-characters-spec` It has the same characters as the IDs in spec 8.2 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L22) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.revision-identifies-terms` \| `revision` \| Yes \| Identifies these terms. An opaque string with the same characters as the IDs in spec 8.2, which the Company changes whenever the terms or `expires_at` change. A `summary` reworded without changing the terms can keep it. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.summary-same-terms` \| `summary` \| No \| The same terms in plain language, written so the User can decide from it alone: what will happen, to what, and any cost, date, or condition _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.basic-markdown-formatting` It MAY use basic Markdown (see "Formatting") [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L25) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.terms-terms-json` \| `terms` \| Yes \| The terms as a JSON object, for the Personal Agent to check and show the User. The Company defines its keys, as with `message.data` (spec 8.4). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L26) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.expires-last-time` \| `expires_at` \| Yes \| The last time an approval of this revision is accepted (RFC 3339). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L27) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.everything-affects-action` Everything that affects the action, such as what it changes, any amount, date, or recipient, or a condition for cancelling, MUST be in the revision's `terms`, and in `summary` if present [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L28) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-perform-what` The Company MUST perform only what the approved revision describes [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L29) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.start-action-before` MUST NOT start the action before it receives an approval for it [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L30) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ops.formatting-summary-text` Formatting. A `summary` is text that MAY use a few CommonMark elements: emphasis (`*italic*`), strong emphasis (`bold`), paragraphs, and lists [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L31) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-render` A Personal Agent MAY render them or show the text as is [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L32) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-render-2` The Personal Agent MUST NOT render links, images, or HTML in a `summary`, and shows them as text, so a `summary` can't send the User elsewhere or load content while they decide [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L33) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.company-returns-same` The Company then returns the same `operation_id` with a new `revision`, and the User needs to approve the new terms _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L34) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.give-different-sets` It MUST NOT give two different sets of terms the same `revision`, so an approval of one revision never applies to other terms [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L35) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `ops.whichever-revision-approved` Whichever revision is approved, the Company MUST perform each operation at most once (7) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L36) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.company-store-operations` A Company doesn't have to store operations that haven't been performed _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L37) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.expiry-expires-leave` Expiry. `expires_at` SHOULD leave the User long enough to read the terms and decide, unless the Company can't hold the terms that long, such as a price or a seat that can sell out [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L38) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Operations 4 Asking for approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.company-wants-approval` A Company that wants approval for an action refuses the request for it, performs nothing, and returns the operation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L41) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.authorization-error-authenticate` It isn't an authorization error, so it doesn't go in `WWW-Authenticate`, and it works the same signed in or out _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L42) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `ops.body-other-members` The body MAY have other members, such as the API's own error fields [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L43) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.tool-returns-error` The tool returns an error result, with `isError` set to `true`, the operation in `operation` in `structuredContent`, and text that says the action needs approval, such as the summary: _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L44) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.browser-kept-login` A browser that kept a login its join didn't give it gets the website's own approval flow instead, because its operations would belong to an account the Session isn't signed in to (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.session-website-handled` `sid` is the `sid` of the Session the website handled the request as (spec 5.2), so the Personal Agent knows which of its Sessions, and which Company, the operation is for _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L46) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.reference-most-2048` `ref` is the reference: at most 2048 characters from A–Z, a–z, 0–9, `-`, `_`, and `.` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L47) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-chooses-form` The Company chooses its form _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L48) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.works-session-approve` It works in any Session that can approve the operation (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L49) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-website-offer` The Company's website SHOULD offer a way to make the original request again, such as a Continue button on the page that's waiting, so the Personal Agent can repeat the action once it's approved (6) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L50) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `ops.action-website-repeat` An action the website can't repeat, such as one guarded by a single-use form token, isn't suited to operations on the website, and the website handles its approval itself _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L51) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.body-whatever-made` The body is for whatever made the request, and doesn't carry the operation, which the Personal Agent gets only from `endpoint` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L52) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.company-website-answer` The Company's website SHOULD answer a page load or form submission with a page that says the action is waiting for approval in the User's personal agent [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L53) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `ops.company-website-answer-2` The Company's website SHOULD answer a request from its own scripts that accepts JSON, such as a `fetch`, with a JSON object with `error` set to `approval_required`, like an API's but without the operation [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L54) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `ops.object-other-members` The object MAY have other members, such as the website's own error fields: [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L55) | MAY | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-take` The Personal Agent MUST take a reference only from the `Poppy-Operation` header of a response that its own browser received, never from page content or a message, and only when `sid` names a Session it joined that browser to [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L56) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 5 Approving an operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ops.request-returns-operation` When a request returns an operation, the Personal Agent MUST NOT treat the action as done [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L59) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.user-approved-personal` User approved: the Personal Agent asks the User, and the User approves _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.agent-approved-personal` Agent approved: the Personal Agent approves on an instruction the User gave it, such as "go ahead with any exchange under $20" _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L61) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-show` The Personal Agent MUST show the User the Company's name and the revision's terms [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L62) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.take-user-answer` MUST take the User's answer through its own interface [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L63) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.treat-text-company` It MUST NOT treat text from the Company, such as a conversation message, as the User's approval [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L64) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-describe` The Personal Agent can describe the terms itself, or show the values in `terms` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L65) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.operation-summary-personal` When the operation has a `summary`, the Personal Agent SHOULD show it rather than write its own description [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L66) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.rest-instruction-user` It MUST rest on an instruction the User gave the Personal Agent [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L67) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.content-company-website` Content from the Company, a website, or anything else the Personal Agent read isn't one, even when it says it comes from the User _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L68) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.before-approving-personal` Before approving, the Personal Agent MUST check the revision's terms against that instruction, and approve only if the instruction covers them [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L69) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.extension` This extension doesn't say how _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L70) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-tell` If the Personal Agent can't tell whether it does, it asks the User _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L71) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.company-answers-personal` If the Company answers the Personal Agent's agent approval with a new revision (6), or a website returns a new operation for the action after recording it, the Personal Agent MUST NOT approve the new one on the same instruction [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L72) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `ops.before-approving-personal-2` Before approving, the Personal Agent SHOULD check that `terms` agree with what it asked for, and with the `summary` if there is one, and point out any difference to the User when it asks them [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L73) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.company-writes-both` The Company writes both, so the `summary` alone could describe something other than the `terms` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L74) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.website-what-asked` On a website, what it asked for is the action its browser just took (8.2) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L75) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.approval-covers-revision` An approval covers one revision _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L76) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.revision-arrives-needs` When a new revision arrives, it needs a new approval, from the User or the Personal Agent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L77) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.user-prefers-earlier` If the User prefers an earlier revision, the Personal Agent can send its approval, but the Company may have replaced it (6) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L78) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.user-withdraws-approval` If the User withdraws their approval, or the instruction an agent approval rests on, before the Personal Agent has sent it, the Personal Agent doesn't send it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L79) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 6 Sending the approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-include` The Personal Agent MUST include `approver` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L82) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.approved-unix-seconds` `approved_at`, in Unix seconds: when the User approved, with `user`, or when the Personal Agent approved, with `agent` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L83) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.earlier-request-example` It can be earlier than the request, for example when the Personal Agent sends the approval later _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L84) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.input-type-user` `input_type`, only with `user`: how the User gave their answer, as a short string, such as `tap`, `typed`, or `voice` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L85) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-include-2` The Personal Agent MUST NOT include it with `agent`, and a Company ignores it there [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L86) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.reference-personal-agent` `reference`: an ID for the Personal Agent's own record of the approval, such as an entry in a ledger the User can see, so the Company and the Personal Agent's operator can look into the approval later _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L87) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.opaque-same-characters` It is opaque, has the same characters as the IDs in spec 8.2, and is unique among the User's approvals at least _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L88) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-send` The Personal Agent MUST NOT send the same `reference` to two Companies, so that Companies can't use it to link the User's approvals at one Company to their approvals at another [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L89) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.personal-agent-personal` The Personal Agent MUST NOT put personal data, or anything that identifies the User or their device, in `input_type` or `reference` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L90) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.include-approved-input` It SHOULD include `approved_at` and `input_type` with `user` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L91) | SHOULD | both |  |
| – | `ops.company-record-approver` A Company MAY record `approver`, `approved_at`, `input_type` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L92) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.reference-reject-decline` `reference`, and MUST NOT reject or decline an approval because an optional member is missing or because it doesn't recognize the `input_type` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L93) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.idempotency-draft-ietf` An `Idempotency-Key` (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header) sent with the first request doesn't carry over: the request with the approval has its own, or none _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L94) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.companies-ignore-members` Companies MUST ignore members of `Poppy-Approval` they don't recognize, so later versions can add members [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L95) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.message-text-approve` The message's `text` doesn't approve anything, whatever it says _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L96) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-accept-approval` The Company MUST NOT accept an approval of a website's operation at an API, MCP server, or conversation, or an approval of another interface's operation at `endpoint` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L97) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ops.website-make-again` The website MAY make it again itself, such as from a page that waits for the approval [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L98) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.otherwise-handles-request` Otherwise, it handles the request as one without an approval, and returns a new reference as in section 4 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L99) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-keep-recorded` The Company MUST keep a recorded approval that isn't used up until the approved revision's `expires_at` [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L100) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.apply-requests-session` MUST NOT apply it to requests from a Session that can't approve the operation [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L101) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.looking-approved-operation` Looking up an approved operation. Once an operation has a recorded approval, a request to `endpoint` with its reference and no approval responds with HTTP 200 and the operation's state in `status`: `approved` while the approval waits for the browser's request, `performing` while the Company performs the action or doesn't yet know whether it took effect, and `performed` after _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L102) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.after-session-header` After the Session header checks in spec 5.3 and the token checks in spec 7, the Company MUST make the following checks before performing the action, and respond as the first one that fails says, whatever order it makes them in internally: [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L103) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.company-compares-what` The Company compares what the requests mean, not their bytes, and MAY ignore differences it considers inconsequential, such as the order of JSON members [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L104) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `ops.treat-revision-replaced` It MAY treat a revision it has replaced with a later one as failing this check [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L105) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.check-fails-performs` If check 3 fails, it performs nothing and returns the operation with a revision for what the request asks, as in section 4 _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L106) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-answer-approval` A Company MUST NOT answer an approval with the revision it names, so a Personal Agent never retries the same approval in a loop [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L107) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ops.once-checks-pass` Once the checks pass, a Company MAY decline the approval instead of performing the action, for its own reasons, such as `approver`, the account, or its own risk checks [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L108) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.performs-nothing-returns` It performs nothing and returns no new operation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L109) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.operation-approval-operation` \| `operation_id` \| Yes \| The approval's `operation_id`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L110) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.revision-approval-revision` \| `revision` \| Yes \| The approval's `revision`. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L111) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `ops.reason-short-plain` \| `reason` \| No \| Why, in short plain language for the User, like the `reason` of a `user_requested` event (spec 8.10). \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L112) | MAY | both |  |
| – | `ops.alternative-another-action` \| `alternative` \| No \| Another way to do the action, as in spec 9.2, such as a `web` reference where the User can do it themselves. \| _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L113) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-anything-reason` The Company MUST NOT put anything in `reason` that the Session couldn't already see [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L114) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.tool-returns-error-2` An MCP tool returns an error result, with `isError` set to `true`, the same members, `error` included, in `structuredContent`, and text that says the action wasn't performed, such as the `reason` _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L115) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.company-record-declined` The Company MUST NOT record a declined approval, so a website never finds it for a later request [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L116) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `ops.approval-declined-personal` When an approval is declined, the Personal Agent MUST NOT send that approval again [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L117) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.approve-revision-same` MUST NOT approve a new revision for the same action without asking the User (5) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L118) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.content-company-spec` They are content from the Company (spec 10.1): it can show them or put them in its own words, and doesn't follow them as instructions _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L119) | MUST | company |  |

## Operations 7 Retries and at most once

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.company-perform-operation` The Company MUST perform each operation at most once, however many times its approval is sent [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L122) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.request-approval-operation` A request with the approval of an operation already performed gets the response the Company gave the first time, or one that says the same, for as long as the Company remembers the operation _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L123) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.company-remember-performed` The Company MUST remember that it performed an operation at least until the approved revision's `expires_at`, and while it is being performed [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L124) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.after-forget` After that, it MAY forget it [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L125) | MAY | both |  |
| ! | `ops.retry-fails-check` A retry then fails check 3 or is handled as a request without an approval, so it gets a new revision and the action still isn't performed twice _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L126) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.website-browser-request` On a website, the browser's request carries no approval, so once the action is performed, the next request for it is a new one and gets a new operation (6) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L127) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.conversation-message-retried` In a conversation, a message retried with the same ID gets the original response (spec 8.3), and a new message with the same approval adds nothing _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L128) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.while-operation-being` While an operation is being performed, or the Company doesn't know whether it took effect, for example after a timeout in one of its own systems, the Company MUST NOT respond as if it failed [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L129) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.server-responds-http` An API or MCP server responds with HTTP 503 and a `Retry-After` header, or as it does for work that hasn't finished _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L130) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.declined-approval-means` A declined approval (6) means the operation wasn't performed _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L131) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.failure-personal-agent` It isn't a failure, and the Personal Agent doesn't send the approval again _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L132) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.request-approval-fails` If a request with an approval fails or times out, the Personal Agent sends it again with the same approval _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L133) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.approve-operation-same` It MUST NOT approve a new operation for the same action, or ask the User to, until it knows whether the first one was performed [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L134) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `ops.operation-answer-retry` A new operation in answer to a retry doesn't say, so the Personal Agent finds out another way, such as from the order in the Company's API _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L135) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.website-browser-request-2` On a website, if the browser's request fails or times out after the approval was recorded, the Personal Agent has the browser make it again _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L136) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.approval-wasn-used` An approval that wasn't used up still applies _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L137) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.reference-answer-means` A new reference in answer means the approval was used up or no longer matches _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L138) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.before-approving-asking` Before approving the new one, or asking the User about it, the Personal Agent looks up the earlier reference at `endpoint` (6): while it is `performing`, it waits, and when it is `performed`, it doesn't approve it _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L139) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 8.1 What an approval proves

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `ops.company-revoke-client` A Company MAY revoke the `client_id` of a Personal Agent that sends an approval the User didn't give or instruct (spec 4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L142) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.company-chooses-actions` A Company chooses which actions it returns operations for (1) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L143) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.action-where-wants` For an action where it wants to see the User approve, it doesn't return operations, and has the User confirm on its own website or in its app, signed in, the way Direct Sign-In works _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L144) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `ops.extension-define-step` This extension doesn't define that step, which differs from operations on a website (4): those are approved by the Personal Agent _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L145) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.accepting-user-approvals` Accepting only `user` approvals still relies on the Personal Agent's statement, and doesn't show that the User approved _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L146) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.would-another-member` It would be another member of a user approval, which Companies that don't support it ignore _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L147) | MUST | company |  |

## Operations 8.2 Operations on websites

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.reference-credential-either` A reference isn't a credential either: it gets an operation only in a Session that can approve it (3) _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L150) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.poppy-operation-either` The `sid` in `Poppy-Operation` isn't one either _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L151) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `ops.terms-come-company` The terms come from the Company, so the User sees the real terms, but the Personal Agent SHOULD check that the operation is for the action its browser just took, and point out any difference to the User, as with `terms` (5) [↗](pap-0.4/ext-operations.md#L152) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: Handling secrets

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.access-tokens-refresh` Access tokens and refresh tokens [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L7) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.private-keys-client` Private keys, client assertions, Session JWTs, and DPoP proofs [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L8) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.authorization-codes-pkce` Authorization codes, PKCE code verifiers, device codes, one-time sign-in codes, browser-session codes, and credentials sent in mediated sign-in [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L9) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-logs-telemetry` Keep them out of logs, telemetry, error reports, model context, conversation messages, and URLs. Tokens and Session JWTs MUST NOT be sent in a URL (5.6), and tokens, Session JWTs, private keys, authorization codes, PKCE code verifiers, and device codes MUST NOT go in model context (10.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L10) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `guide.redact-authorization-poppy` Redact the `Authorization`, `Poppy-Session`, `DPoP`, and `Cookie` headers and credential fields before a request reaches a logger or tracer [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L11) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.send-cache-control` Send `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response that carries a token or code [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L12) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: Signing and verifying JWTs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.personal-agents-sign` Personal agents: sign Session JWTs with ES256 (MUST, 5.2). Sign client assertions and delegations with ES256, or with PS384 if you sign them blindly (10.7). Companies: accept ES256 (MUST) and PS384 (SHOULD) in client assertions and delegations (4.1, 5.2). Use RSA keys of at least 2048 bits [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L15) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-token` Personal agents: use `token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported` in the Company's OAuth metadata to choose a supported client-assertion algorithm. This list does not establish support for delegation signatures. The protocol has no delegation-algorithm discovery field, and `invalid_session` does not distinguish an unsupported algorithm from other failures. An agent that requires blind signing may be unable to work with a Company that doesn't support PS384. Falling back to ES256 needs a suitable published key and gives up this blind-signing mechanism; don't switch automatically when blind signing is required by the User's privacy settings [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L16) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `guide.reject-none-symmetric` Reject `alg: none` and symmetric algorithms such as HS256 [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L17) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.verify-client-assertions` Verify client assertions and delegations only with keys from the personal agent's verified `jwks_uri` (4.1), and Session JWTs only with the key their verified delegation names in `cnf.jwk` (5.2). Ignore `jku`, `x5u`, and any other key embedded in a JWT. DPoP proofs for DPoP-bound access tokens are the one other exception: the public key in their `jwk` header is how they work [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L18) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.check-client-assertions` Check `aud` and `iat`, and `exp` on client assertions and delegations. Session JWTs have no `exp`: accept them only within your `iat` window (5.3). A client assertion has the company's issuer as its `aud`; a Session JWT has the Company's identifier (its issuer, or its HTTPS domain without one), never an endpoint URL (4.1, 5.2). Allow a small clock skew, such as 30 seconds, and reject assertions that claim a long lifetime [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L19) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.make-client-assertion` Make the `jti` of each client assertion, delegation, Session JWT, and DPoP proof at least 128 random bits, and each Session ID too [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L20) | SHOULD | both |  |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-client` Personal agents: set a client assertion's `exp` at most five minutes after its `iat` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L21) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `guide.companies-reject-reused` Companies: reject a reused client assertion `jti` from the same `client_id` until it expires, as RFC 7523 §3 allows [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L22) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Operator signatures and bot defenses

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.build-request-body` Build the request body, any DPoP proof, and Session JWT first, then the operator signature. Cover `poppy-session` and `authorization` when present, as the spec requires. Include method, authority, path, query, and a verified content digest when the verifier relies on those components [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L25) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-operator-keys` Keep operator keys separate from delegated Session keys. Publishing every User's delegated key in an operator directory is not equivalent to verifying a delegation, and exposes a new key mapping [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L26) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.centralized-agent-signing` For a centralized agent, signing can happen where requests already pass. For on-device agents, sending requests to an authenticated operator signing service can reveal which Company each User visits. This signature profile does not provide blind signing. Do not send devices a shared operator private key to avoid that service [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L27) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.verified-operator-signature` A verified operator signature establishes control of its key source. It does not establish every client metadata URL on the same origin. Verify the Session JWT's exact `iss` before accepting it as that client, then apply Company policy and account authorization [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L28) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.test-actual-edge` Test the actual edge and origin together: registration, directory caching, key rotation, accepted signature components, body handling, and forwarded authentication results. Protect the origin from forged forwarding headers. A bot-verification result is not a replay check or account grant [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L29) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.remove-extra-signature` Remove the extra signature where an edge verifies delegated Session JWTs directly. Keep Company acceptance and all remaining Session and OAuth checks. The JWT covers method, URL without query, and access token, not the request body; do not assume removing an operator signature preserves any additional query or body protection it supplied [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L30) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: Rotating keys

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.give-every-jwks` Give every key in `jwks_uri` a `kid` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L33) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.publish-jwks-before` Publish a new key in `jwks_uri` before signing with it, early enough for companies' caches to pick it up [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L34) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-public-published` Keep an old public key published until every client assertion and delegation signed with it has expired [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L35) | SHOULD | both |  |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-rotate` Personal agents: rotate delegated keys as often as you like. Each Session JWT carries its own delegation, so companies don't depend on a delegated key lasting (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L36) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-rotate-2` Personal agents: rotate DPoP keys as often as you like too, but use each one for one user ID only (MUST, 4.5). Send a proof with the new key when you refresh, and the new access token is bound to it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L37) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `guide.companies-refetch-jwks` Companies refetch `jwks_uri` when they see an unknown `kid`. The refetch happens before any signature is checked, so anyone can trigger it by naming a real personal agent and a made-up `kid`. Refetch each `jwks_uri` at most once per interval, such as 30 seconds, and count failed fetches too. Otherwise a stream of bad assertions can flood the personal agent's server [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L38) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.rotating-signing-keys` Rotating signing keys doesn't affect refresh tokens. They are tied to the `client_id`, not a key (4.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L39) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: Fetching metadata safely

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.limits-redirects-most` Set limits: a few redirects at most, a response size such as 100 KB, and a timeout of a few seconds [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L42) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.validate-https-certificates` Validate HTTPS certificates. Personal agents MUST follow discovery redirects only to HTTPS URLs (section 3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L43) | MUST | both |  |
| ✓ | `guide.metadata-no-credentials` Never send cookies, tokens, or other credentials on these fetches [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L44) | SHOULD | both | `guide/metadata-fetch-credentials` |
| ✓ | `guide.private-addresses` Reject loopback, private, and link-local addresses unless you've configured them on purpose. Check the address you actually connect to, not only the one DNS returned first [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L45) | SHOULD | both | `identity/private-agent-urls`<br>_on Node the metadata fetch checks the address it connects to (packages/core/src/safe-fetch.ts); core unit test packages/core/test/safe-fetch.test.ts_ |
| ✎ | `guide.cache-bounds` Cache according to HTTP caching headers, within bounds you set, such as at least a minute and at most a day. The upper bound means a removed key stops being trusted [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L46) | SHOULD | both | _client metadata is cached for its max-age, between a minute and a day; core unit test packages/core/test/client-cache.test.ts_ |

## Guides: Explicit replies and approvals

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.both-parties-make` Both parties SHOULD make an answer or approval explicit about the question or action it addresses [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L49) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.both-parties-treat` Both parties SHOULD treat a short reply that could answer more than one open question as answering none of them, and ask which one is meant before acting. A reply such as "done" could refer to sign-in, an earlier question, or a new request for approval [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L50) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: Retries

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.send-idempotency-draft` Send an `Idempotency-Key` (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header) on API writes that accept one. Use a random UUID (version 4), and reuse the same key when you retry the same request [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L53) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.give-conversation-request` Give each conversation request, such as a message or a handoff request, an `id` with at least 128 random bits, and reuse it when you retry the request (8.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L54) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.retry-needs-session` Each retry needs a new Session JWT, and a new DPoP proof if the access token is DPoP-bound. A retried token request needs a new assertion. The company may reject a `jti` it has already seen [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L55) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.wait-least-long` Wait at least as long as `Retry-After` says on a 429 (MUST, 5.6) or a 503 [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `guide.otherwise-back-exponentially` Otherwise, back off exponentially with jitter, cap the delay, and limit the number of attempts [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L57) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.companies-keep-idempotency` Companies keep idempotency records for a set time, such as a day, scoped to the personal agent's `client_id` and the user ID, and to the account when there is one, not to the session, so a retry in a new session still matches. They return the original response for a repeated key, and reject a repeated key with a different body [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L58) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Rate limits

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.companies-limit-client` Companies: limit by `client_id`, by user, and by session, so one busy personal agent or user doesn't crowd out others. Count a request against a `client_id` only after its Session JWT or client assertion's signature checks pass. Otherwise anyone can name a personal agent and use up its limit, so its real users are refused. Limit unverified requests by network instead [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L61) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.companies-send-ratelimit` Companies: also send the `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers (IETF draft), so personal agents can slow down before they hit a limit [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L62) | SHOULD | company |  |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-keep` Personal agents: keep track of limits for each company and share them across your tasks and users, rather than letting each task find the limit on its own [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L63) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-prefer` Personal agents: prefer long polling or streaming over repeated short polls, and check for changes no more often than the task needs. Checking once a day for a price drop is usually enough [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L64) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.personal-agents-work` Personal agents: run work that isn't time-sensitive, such as checking order status in the background, outside the company's busy hours, and spread it out instead of starting it all at the same moment [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L65) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Transport and JSON

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.later-prefer` Use TLS 1.2 or later. Prefer TLS 1.3 [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L68) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.encode-json-reject` Encode JSON as UTF-8 and reject objects with duplicate member names [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L69) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.write-timestamps-3339` Write timestamps in RFC 3339 with a time zone offset, such as `2026-10-02T17:15:00-07:00` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L70) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.ignore-fields-recognize` Ignore fields you don't recognize, so later versions can add them [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L71) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: User IDs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.store-random-user` Store a random ID for each user and company the first time they're needed. This is the simplest choice [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L74) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.derive-keyed-hash` Derive one with a keyed hash, such as HMAC-SHA256 of your internal user ID and the company's identifier (its issuer, or its HTTPS domain without one), with a secret key. Changing the key changes every ID, so the company sees all your users as new [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L75) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.create-random-anonymous` Create a random ID for each anonymous browsing session. Its sessions have their own `sid`, and its delegated keys sign for no other user ID (5.2), so nothing links it to the user's other sessions [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L76) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.discard-browsing-session` Discard the ID when the browsing session ends. Carts and conversations from it end with it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L77) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.never-send-access` Never send an access token with an anonymous ID (MUST NOT, 5.4). If the user wants to sign in, switch to their regular ID in a new session [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L78) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: The Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.decide-where-send` Decide where to send the header from the company's `poppy.json` and its listed API descriptions (5.2). For OpenAPI, resolve the request URL from the operation's server and path. For MCP, use the listed server endpoint and its transport's request URLs. For conversations, use the listed endpoint and the routes in 8.2. Other protocol and extension endpoints follow their definitions, such as `tasks.endpoint`, the `feedback.endpoint` its response lists, and `{browser_session_endpoint}/authorize`. Match the request to those operations and routes before signing. A host allowlist alone would include unrelated paths on a shared host [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L81) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.fetch-discovery-documents` Fetch discovery documents, API descriptions, and other public documents without the Session header. Keep it off OAuth requests too. A web link in an alternative or message doesn't add a destination. The JWT's `aud` identifies the company, while `htu` binds it to the request URL. Neither chooses where to send it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L82) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.fetch-website-page` When you fetch a website page yourself, without a browser, send the header if the page is on the host that served `poppy.json` (SHOULD, 5.2), never with an access token. Sign a new one for a redirect only while it stays on that host. A browser, headless or not, joins the session instead (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L83) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.page-answers-invalid` If a page answers `invalid_session`, treat it as a bug in your header, as at any endpoint, and check the JWT. You can fetch the page again without the header in the meantime (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L84) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.choose-session-random` Choose each session's `sid` at random, and never use it for another session (MUST, 5.2). Keep it for as long as you use the session: it names the session, so a lost `sid` means a new session [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L85) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.send-same-agent` Send the same `sub` and `agent_id` in every Session JWT for a session (MUST, 5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L86) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.sign-session-request` Sign a new Session JWT for each request, in an HTTP client hook that sees the final method and URL. Don't let the client follow redirects from protocol endpoints with the Session header or a token: you MUST NOT send either to the new URL (section 3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L87) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.generate-delegated-keys` Generate delegated keys where you sign, and make them non-extractable where your platform allows, such as in a key management service, WebCrypto, or the device's keystore. Use each one for one user ID only (MUST, 5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L88) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.delegation-before-current` Get a new delegation before the current one expires. You MUST NOT sign a Session JWT after its delegation's `exp` (5.2). Round its `iat` down, such as to the start of the hour, and set `exp` from the rounded value, so delegations issued together can't be matched by their times. Keep its lifetime to a few hours [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L89) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.never-expose-private` Never expose private keys to a model or to tools a model can call. Sign on the model's behalf in code it can't reach [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L90) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.request-gets-session` When a request gets `session_ended`, start a new session with a new `sid` and send the request again (MUST, 5.5). The old session's cart and browser cookie don't carry over, so tell the user if a cart is lost. On `invalid_session`, don't start a new session: it would fail the same way. Check the JWT instead, such as its delegation's `exp`, `htu`, and the clock [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L91) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-issues-dpop` If a company issues DPoP-bound access tokens, also sign a DPoP proof for each request that carries one, and support nonces as RFC 9449 §8 describes. The proof and the Session JWT are separate signatures with separate keys (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L92) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Storing tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.store-refresh-tokens` Store refresh tokens as secrets (10.2). Encrypt them at rest, apart from the model and its tools. Give tools a reference to the token, not the token [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L95) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.keep-access-tokens` Keep access tokens in memory and drop them when they expire [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L96) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.refresh-token-tied` A refresh token is tied to your `client_id`, not to a DPoP key (RFC 9449 §5), so whoever holds it and your client private key can use it. Keep the client private key in a key service or hardware security module that signs without exporting it, and store refresh tokens apart from it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L97) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.store-refresh-tokens-2` Store refresh tokens by the company's full issuer, as for user IDs, so a token from one company hosted by a provider is never sent to another [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L98) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.before-first-signed` Before the first signed-in call to a service, fetch its protected resource metadata. If it has some and its `resource` isn't `https://{organization.domain}`, request a token for that `resource` and use that token only there (4.5). Cache the metadata by its HTTP caching headers, and fetch it again when the service answers `invalid_token` with `resource_metadata` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L99) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.server-always-token` At an MCP server, always use a token whose `resource` is the server's `url` (MUST, section 7), with the scheme `token_type` names. Send the Session header there too: the server may ignore it, but you can't tell in advance [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L100) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-returns-refresh` When the company returns a new refresh token, you MUST use it from then on (4.4). Replace the stored one right away. When a refresh response omits it, keep the existing refresh token [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L101) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.after-user-signs` After the user signs in again for more scopes, revoke the old refresh token (4.7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L102) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.invalid-grant-refresh` On `invalid_grant` for a refresh token, continue signed out: send the Session header without an access token (5.5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L103) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.session-second-account` Use a new session for a second account (5.4), keeping its tasks and browser cookie separate from the first account's [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L104) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Choosing how to sign in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.before-asking-user` Before asking the user to sign in, check whether a refresh token you hold already covers the task (5.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L107) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.offer-sign-company` Don't offer sign-in at a company that sets `auth.disabled` (MUST, 3.2). When a company refuses a sign-in type with `unauthorized_client`, continue signed out, tell the user the company doesn't offer that sign-in to you, and remember the refusal for a while rather than asking the user again on the next task (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L108) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.prefer-direct-device` Prefer direct or device sign-in to mediated sign-in (SHOULD, Mediated Sign-In 6), and direct to device sign-in (SHOULD, 4). With direct and device sign-in, the user's password stays with the company [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L109) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.scopes-supported-issuer` Use `scopes_supported` from the issuer's metadata and from the domain's protected resource metadata, the company's OpenAPI description, and its sign-in extension metadata to find scopes. The advertised list may be incomplete. Read descriptions where available to pick the ones the task needs (4.7); a missing description or hint says nothing about whether a scope is safe to request automatically [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L110) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.auth-scope-hints` Use `auth.scope_hints` to decide which scopes need the user's go-ahead before you request them (4.7). For example, request a scope whose `changes` is `irreversible`, or whose `personal_data` is `true`, only when the user agreed to that kind of access, and let the user set that preference once rather than for every sign-in. Treat a scope without hints as `irreversible` with personal data [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L111) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.hints-describe-whole` Hints describe a whole scope. The consequences of one action still come from the action itself, such as an MCP tool's annotations, or the HTTP method: a `GET` doesn't change anything [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L112) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.fewest-scopes-task` Ask for the fewest scopes the task needs, not every scope the company offers. For a task that only looks things up, request a read-only access token with a broader refresh token (4.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L113) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-approve-fewer` The user may approve fewer scopes than you asked for. Check `scope` in the response before continuing. A response without `scope` granted every scope you asked for [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L114) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-grant-scope` A company may also not grant a scope to this user at all, for example when only the account holder can allow an action (4.7). You can't tell that apart from the user leaving it out. When a sign-in comes back without a scope the task needs, don't send the user to sign in again just for it. Tell them that access wasn't granted, and that if they didn't leave it out, someone else on the account, such as the account holder, may need to do the task [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L115) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Direct and device sign-in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.direct-device-sign` Use direct or device sign-in only when the user signs in themselves (MUST, 5.4). Never type the user's password, enter their one-time code, or click the company's approval controls for them [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L118) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.open-authorization-user` Open the authorization URL in the user's own browser, not in a browser you automate [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L119) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.make-state-random` Make `state` random and single-use. Record which company it belongs to, and exchange the code only at that company's `token_endpoint`. Check that the redirect's `iss` matches that company's issuer (MUST, 4.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L120) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.pkce-code-challenge` Use PKCE with `code_challenge_method=S256`, as RFC 9700 §2.1.1 recommends [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L121) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.receive-redirect-device` If you can't receive the redirect on the device the user is talking to you on, send the authorization URL to the user, for example to their phone, with a redirect URI you control. Fall back to device sign-in only when that isn't possible (4.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L122) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.device-sign-show` For device sign-in (4.3), show `verification_uri_complete` as a link or QR code, and show `user_code` too so the user can confirm it matches. Keep `device_code` private. Show the link only if its host is the company's issuer host or `organization.domain`, or a subdomain of either, and show the company's name and domain with it (MUST, 4.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L123) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.poll-faster-interval` Poll no faster than `interval`. On `slow_down`, add 5 seconds to the interval, as RFC 8628 describes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L124) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Mediated sign-in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.collect-extension-fields` Collect the extension's `fields` in a form that sends them straight to your sign-in code, so secret values never pass through the model [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L127) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.look-stored-credentials` Look up stored credentials by the company's issuer, and show the company's name and domain on the form and when asking for a code (MUST, Mediated Sign-In 6). Field labels come from the company and can name anything [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L128) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.secret-fields-never` Secret fields MUST never be shown back to the user, logged, or sent anywhere other than the token endpoint of the company's issuer (Mediated Sign-In 2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L129) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.after-sign-ends` After a sign-in ends, you MUST either discard the credentials or keep them only in a credential store the user chose, such as a password manager (Mediated Sign-In 6). If you discard them and the user needs to sign in again later, ask again [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L130) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.after-user-disconnects` After the user disconnects you or the company revokes your access, don't sign in again with stored credentials unless the user asks you to [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L131) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.code-required-tell` On `code_required`, tell the user where the code was sent, using `sent_to`, ask for it, and send only the code with `sign_in_id` (Mediated Sign-In 4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L132) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Native and distributed apps

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.signing-private-distribute` Don't put your signing private key in an app you distribute. Anyone could extract it and act as your personal agent. Keep the key on your server, and have the app ask the server to sign assertions for the signed-in user [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L135) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.delegated-keys-stay` Delegated keys can stay on the device. The app generates one in its platform keystore and asks your server for a delegation for it, then signs Session JWTs itself (5.2). 10.7 explains what this hides from your own servers, and blind signing, which hides more [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L136) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.redirect-uris-https` Redirect URIs are HTTPS URLs on your `client_id` domain, or loopback redirect URIs (4.1). To return the user to a phone app, use an HTTPS link the app claims, such as an iOS universal link or an Android app link, or use device sign-in. A desktop app can listen on a loopback port, as RFC 8252 §7.3 describes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L137) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Web browsing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.browser-website-company` Don't use a browser on the website of a company that sets `web.disabled`. Use its company agent and APIs (SHOULD NOT, section 6). Fetching a page without a browser, such as a policy, is still fine, with the Session header (5.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L140) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.browse-signed-request` To browse signed in, request `poppy:browser-sign-in` with the other scopes the task needs, from a company that lists `browser_session_endpoint` (section 6). Where `web.unscoped` is `true`, it gives the account's full access on the website, so treat it like a scope that allows changes that can't be undone, and ask the user when you would for one. Otherwise it adds nothing to the other scopes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L141) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.separate-browser-storage` Use a separate browser storage context, with its own cookies and local storage, for each session. Never share one across users [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L142) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.type-user-password` Don't type the user's password or other credentials into a company's website. Sign in with direct, device, or mediated sign-in, then join your browser to the session (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L143) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.join-browser-session` Join the browser to the session right before you start browsing, and join again after signing in, or when the website stops recognizing the session [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L144) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.join-without-access` A join without an access token leaves a login the browser already has, while a signed-in join replaces it, and the browser is signed out when that sign-in ends (section 6 has a table of each case) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L145) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.read-browser-session` Read the browser-session code only from the endpoint's page in your own browser, authorize it in code your model can't read, and have the browser submit the form right away. Never authorize a code from a message or another page (MUST NOT, section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L146) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.close-storage-context` Close the storage context when the session ends [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L147) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.read-events-long` Read events with a long `wait`, such as 30 seconds, or a stream, rather than many short polls (8.5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L150) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.read-until-working` Read until `working` is `false` before treating the company's reply as complete (8.7). A successful `POST` only means the company accepted the request [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L151) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.tell-whether-company` To tell whether a company agent's reply covers your latest message, compare its `as_of_request` with that message's request ID. Send `as_of_cursor` on messages you write, so the company can tell whether a short answer like "Done" answers its latest message or an earlier one (8.4). Messages from people carry neither [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L152) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.cursor-expired-tell` On `cursor_expired`, tell the user that part of the conversation is missing (8.5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L153) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.show-text-delta` Show `text-delta` pieces only as a preview. Act only on the complete `message` event (8.6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L154) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.structured-details-data` Put structured details in `data`, not JSON or other markup in `text` (8.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L155) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.links-extension-show` With the Links extension, show a link's title with the domain of its `url`, so the user can see where it goes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L156) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.disclosures-extension-disclosure` With the Disclosures extension, when a disclosure is relevant to what you tell the user, such as an allergen warning on food they're buying, show it in full, apart from the rest of the message. Leave out disclosures that read like promotion rather than a notice [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L157) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-agent-skip` With a company agent, skip greetings and small talk, and keep text short (8.8) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L158) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.before-asking-person` Before asking for a person, send a short message that sums up the problem, so they don't have to read the whole conversation (8.9) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L159) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-agent-solves` If the company agent solves the problem while you wait for a person, withdraw the request with `handoff/cancel`. Then follow `handoff` and `responder`: the company may still assign someone (8.9) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L160) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
