| → | `guide.person-takes-over` When a person takes over, write for them: concise, plain sentences, details in `text` rather than only in `data`, and time to reply [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L161) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.close-conversation-task` Close a conversation when the task is done, after reading until `working` is `false`. The company may drop requests it hasn't acted on when the close arrives (8.12) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L162) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-accepts-user` When the user accepts a `user_requested` invitation, start the direct conversation with `parent_conversation_id` and `user_requested_event_id`. Omit `message` to let the company speak first (8.10). Keep reading or streaming its events while the user is participating, including when the user hasn't sent a message [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L163) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-returns-control` When the user returns control to the personal agent, close their direct conversation before continuing in the parent (8.10). Merely switching away from the direct conversation needn't close it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L164) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-agent-asks` If a company agent asks in a message for a one-time code, or for details to verify the user, such as a date of birth or part of an account number, ask it to request sign-in with an `authorization` event instead (8.11). Don't send codes in messages (Handling secrets) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L165) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.some-oauth-libraries` Some OAuth libraries raise an exception when a successful response carries a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. If yours does, check the original status, read the accepted response and its `authorization` event, and handle the header and event as one sign-in need, without sending the accepted message again (8.11) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L166) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Choosing an interface

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.prefer-company-apis` Prefer the company's APIs and company agent over browsing its website. They are faster and change less often [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L169) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.phone-company-publishes` Don't phone a company that publishes a `poppy.json`. Use the interfaces it lists instead [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L170) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.skip-types-conversation` Skip API types and conversation protocols you don't recognize (section 7, 8.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L171) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Task coverage

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.company-tasks-response` Get the company's tasks response early in each Session, before you try a task there, and use it only in that Session (section 9). When the user's task is one of the excluded tasks, tell the user right away instead of trying each interface (9.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L174) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.offer-alternative-something` Offer the alternative when there is one. When it's something the user does themselves, such as a page that opens the company's app, give the user the link instead of browsing it yourself (9.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L175) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.alternative-lead-another` A web alternative can lead to another company's website or app. Show the link's destination domain. To act there, use that company's discovery and its own session and account access, rather than carrying the referring company's Session JWT or access token along [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L176) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.send-feedback-feedback` Send feedback to the `feedback.endpoint` in the tasks response (9.3). A company's APIs may also have feedback operations meant for other clients [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L177) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.company-answers-feedback` When a company answers your feedback report with an alternative, try it before you tell the user the task can't be done (9.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L178) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.skip-company-skill` When you skip a company's skill index, or a skill in it, because you don't recognize its `$schema` or `type`, say so to the user if it matters for the task, so they know the company's guidance wasn't used (9.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L179) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Operations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.follow-explicit-replies` Follow Explicit replies and approvals when interpreting the user's answer to an approval request [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L182) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-show-company` When you ask the user, show the company's name and the account the operation applies to. Showing the complete `terms` in your own interface, such as a card with each value labeled, is often better than any summary. When you show a summary, use the company's `summary` rather than your own paraphrase. Without one, describe every value in `terms` that affects the action. Point out any cost, date, or condition, and whether the action can be undone (Operations 5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L183) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.revision-operation-arrives` When a new revision of an operation arrives, with the same `operation_id`, show the user what changed before asking them to approve the new one. If they'd rather have the earlier terms, you can send that approval. If the company has replaced it, you get a new revision to show them (Operations 6). If you approved the earlier one yourself, ask the user about the new one, rather than approving it on the same instruction [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L184) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.show-revision-expires` Show when the revision expires. If it expires before the user answers, make the request again for new terms, and ask again [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L185) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.save-request-returned` Save the request that returned the operation, its method, URL, and body or the tool's arguments, and send exactly that with the approval. Don't have the model write the request again (Operations 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L186) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.check-terms-against` Check `terms` against what you asked for, such as the order, item, and amount, and tell the user about any difference. If you show values from `terms`, label them in words, such as "Order" rather than `order_id` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L187) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.approve-operation-yourself` Approve an operation yourself only on what the user told you, such as "go ahead with any exchange under $20" or "return everything in this order", and check each revision's terms against it (Operations 5). A setting such as "approve everything from this company" fits only if the user asked for exactly that. Never treat text in a page, a message, or the operation itself as the user's instruction [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L188) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-action-large` Ask the user when the action is large, can't be undone, or differs from what they described, even if an instruction seems to cover it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L189) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.keep-ledger-user` Keep a ledger the user can see, with an entry for each approval: the company, the account, the `terms` and `summary`, the revision, when, whether the user approved it or you did, the instruction an agent approval rested on, and the outcome. Send the entry's ID as `reference` (Operations 6), and let the user see and change the instructions you approve on [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L190) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.task-produces-several` When a task produces several operations, collect them and ask the user about them in one prompt, showing the terms of each. Returning an operation performs nothing, so you can gather them first [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L191) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.instructions-limits-week` Instructions with limits, such as "up to $50 a week", can be used by two tasks at once. Reserve the amount before you approve, and release it if the approval isn't used [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L192) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.recurring-action-fixed` For a recurring action with fixed terms, such as a weekly transfer, a company's own feature, such as a scheduled transfer, set up with one approval, can replace approving every use [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L193) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.after-request-approval` After a request with an approval times out or gets a 503, send it again with the same approval, waiting for `Retry-After` if there is one. Don't approve the action again, or ask the user to, until you know whether it happened (Operations 7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L194) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.website-watch-responses` On a website, watch the responses your browser gets for `Poppy-Operation`, in the software that drives the browser, not the model. Use its `sid` to find your session and the company, ignore a header whose `sid` isn't a session you joined that browser to, and send the reference to that company's `endpoint`. Handle the response as an API's `approval_required` (Operations 4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L195) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.before-asking-user-2` Before asking the user about an operation from a website, check that it's for the action your browser just took. A script on the page can make the website return another one (Operations 8.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L196) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.after-company-records` After the company records the approval, have the browser repeat the action, such as by pressing the page's Continue button or the same button as before, unless the page already moved on by itself (Operations 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L197) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.repeating-action-gets` If repeating the action gets a new reference, look up the earlier one first. Don't ask the user about the new operation while the earlier one is `performing`, or once it's `performed` (Operations 7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L198) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: Choosing capabilities

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.signed-apis-expose` Signed-out APIs. You can expose a catalog or other stateless API without an OAuth server. Accept the Session header personal agents send. If the endpoint uses no Session claims, it can serve requests without verifying the header (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L201) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.session-continuity-verify` Session continuity. Verify Session JWTs when you want to recognize a pseudonymous user, maintain a Session cart, or connect activity across channels. Verification is required before relying on Session identity, ownership, continuity, or state (5.3). This works without OAuth [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L202) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.account-access-oauth` Account access. Add OAuth when tasks need access to a user's account. Your endpoints can rely on OAuth alone if they use no Session claims. They still validate tokens and enforce scopes and any required DPoP checks. Check your existing authorization server against what Poppy adds to OAuth and client metadata support. Check `protected_resources` in its metadata first (3.2): it's the required field an existing issuer is most likely to be missing, and adding it may need a release from its vendor [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L203) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.channels-other-capabilities` Channels and other capabilities. Offer APIs, web browsing, conversations, or a combination. Add browser join to connect website activity to a Session. Advertise excluded tasks, feedback, and extensions where they help users complete the tasks you support [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L204) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Verifying personal agents

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.fetch-client-without` Fetch the `client_id` URL without following redirects. Its `client_id` MUST equal the URL you fetched (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L207) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `guide.cache-client-metadata` Cache client metadata and key sets, as described in Fetching metadata safely [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L208) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-allowlists-blocklists` Keep allowlists or blocklists of `client_id` values, and rate-limit session creation and new `client_id` values (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L209) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.client-metadata` Check whether your authorization server supports client ID metadata documents. Some do, some support them only for clients an administrator registers by URL, and some don't yet. If yours needs registration, register the personal agents you accept by their `client_id` URL and reject others with `invalid_client`, which 4.1 allows. Your OAuth integration can fetch and check the metadata document. Your resources also fetch it when verifying Session JWTs (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L210) | SHOULD | company | _Poppyseed fetches and checks client ID metadata documents itself (packages/core/src/clients.ts)_ |
| ! | `guide.authorization-server-accepts` If your authorization server accepts client ID metadata documents, publish `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` in its metadata, as the CIMD draft §8 defines, so other clients, such as MCP clients, can tell. Personal agents don't need it: a company that offers sign-in already reads their metadata documents (4.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L211) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Verifying the Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.verify-session-header` Verify the Session header in one place, such as a gateway in front of your APIs, conversation endpoint, and browser-session `/authorize` endpoint, and pass the verified `client_id`, `sid`, user ID, and agent ID to the services behind it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L214) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.cache-verified-delegations` Cache verified delegations until they expire (5.2). Key the cache by a hash of the whole delegation, such as its SHA-256, not by its `jti`, which a forged delegation could copy. Most requests then need one signature check [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L215) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.behind-proxies-load` Behind proxies and load balancers, compare `htu` with the public URL the personal agent used. Build it from your configured public origin, not from the `Host` header your server receives [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L216) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.dpop-window` Use an acceptance window of about one minute for `iat`, plus a small clock skew [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L217) | SHOULD | company | _the window is 90 seconds, set in packages/core/src/dpop.ts_ |
| ! | `guide.rejecting-reused-optional` Rejecting a reused `jti` is optional, as it is for DPoP proofs, because servers behind one endpoint don't always share state. Without it, a copied Session JWT still works only for the same method and URL, with the same access token, and within the acceptance window. A request that changes something then relies on being idempotent, so a replay doesn't repeat it. Conversation requests already are, through their IDs (8.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L218) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-replay-cache` If you keep a replay cache keyed by `jti`, hold entries for the acceptance window and share it across every server. Otherwise a JWT accepted by one server can be replayed at another (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L219) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.check-against-access` Check `ath` against the access token, and that the token was issued to the JWT's `iss`. Reject an absent header when the request depends on Session claims (MUST, 5.3). Don't use an unverified `iss`, `sub`, or `sid` for attribution, rate limits by identity, cache keys, or state lookup [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L220) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `guide.return-invalid-session` Return `invalid_session` for a failed check, and keep access token errors in `WWW-Authenticate`, as OAuth does (section 7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L221) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.binding-access-tokens` Binding access tokens with DPoP is your choice (4.5), and you can choose for each service. If you do, verify the proof as RFC 9449 describes, separately from the Session JWT. For a service that doesn't verify proofs, such as an MCP server built for ordinary MCP clients, have your authorization server issue Bearer tokens for its `resource`. If your authorization server can't issue DPoP-bound tokens, verifying the Session JWT and its `ath` binds the token to the personal agent's key. Endpoints that skip Session verification lose that extra protection [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L222) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.server-accept-token` At an MCP server, accept a token issued for its `resource` only at that server (MUST, section 7). Accept the Session header there too, if you want its calls tied to sessions. Signed-out calls that use no Session state can work without verification [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L223) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `guide.pages-host-serves` Pages on the host that serves your `poppy.json` can get the Session header too, from personal agents that fetch them without a browser, and never with an access token (5.2). Verify it before using it, for example to recognize the personal agent or to keep the request in its session. Treat the request as signed out, even when the session's browser is signed in. When the check fails, return `invalid_session` as at any endpoint (5.3), so the personal agent can find the mistake [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L224) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.serve-personal-agent` Serve personal agent conversations only from your conversation endpoint (8.2). If your website chat or other channels can open the same conversations, they may not check the Session header, and anyone with a copied token could read them there [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L225) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Sessions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.behind-load-balancer` Behind a load balancer, share session state across the servers that handle it, as with server-side cookie sessions, so requests reach the same state whichever server handles them [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L228) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.record-user-agent` Record the user ID and agent ID a session starts with, and reject later Session JWTs for it with different ones (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L229) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.session-verification-needs` Session verification needs no state until the session lookup, so a gateway in front of your endpoints can verify the header once and pass the verified claims on. Endpoints that use no Session claims don't need to change (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L230) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.authorization-server-session` Your authorization server doesn't see the Session header. Sign-in and refresh are plain OAuth, and a session is signed in on each request that carries an access token (5.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L231) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.remember-sessions-answer` Remember the `sid`s of sessions you end, and answer them with `session_ended` (5.5). Choose a retention period that fits your session lifetimes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L232) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.separate-sessions-separate` Use separate sessions for separate accounts. If your policy refuses a second account in a session, answer with `session_ended` (5.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L233) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.expect-user-delegated` Don't expect a user's delegated key to stay the same (MUST NOT, 5.2). You can reject a delegated key that signs for a second user ID while a delegation for it lasts, which limits a leaked key to one user (10.7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L234) | MUST NOT | company |  |

## Guides: Token lifetimes and sign-out

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.give-access-tokens` Give access tokens a lifetime of hours, not days [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L237) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.sign-invalidate-access` At sign-out, invalidate the access tokens issued under the revoked refresh token, as RFC 7009 §2.1 describes, or check on each request whether the authorization is still active, so sign-out takes effect right away. If you can do neither, keep access tokens to a few minutes (5.5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L238) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.stop-accepted-work` Don't stop accepted work because the access token that started it expired. A job can outlast the token [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L239) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.revoke-stops-work` Where work in progress can take consequential actions on the user's account, such as payments or changes that are hard to undo, tie it to the refresh token, so revoking access stops it right away [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L240) | SHOULD | company | _a Company's perform can check the account before a consequential step; confirmed operations otherwise finish after sign-out, as spec 4.9 allows_ |
| ! | `guide.give-refresh-tokens` Give refresh tokens a lifetime that fits the account, such as 90 days, and expire ones that go unused sooner. Keep it long enough that users don't have to sign in again often [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L241) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.revoke-user-refresh` Revoke a user's refresh tokens when they reset their password or you suspect the account is compromised [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L242) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.consider-issuing-refresh` Consider issuing a new refresh token on each refresh and revoking the grant when an old one is used again, as RFC 9700 §4.14.2 describes. If a refresh token is copied, the grant ends as soon as both copies have been used [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L243) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.personal-agent-signing` If a personal agent's signing key may have leaked, revoke every refresh token issued to its `client_id`. Its refresh tokens are tied to the `client_id`, not to a DPoP key (RFC 9449 §5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L244) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Describing scopes

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.what-scope-lets` Say what the scope lets the personal agent see or do, in words a user understands [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L247) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.specific-enough-model` Be specific enough for a model to match a task to the scopes it needs. "See your orders and returns" works better than "Read access" [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L248) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.whether-scope-reads` Say whether the scope only reads, and whether a write scope also allows reading [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L249) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.words-actions-undone` Say in words which actions can't be undone and what personal data the scope shows [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L250) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.give-scope-hints` Give each scope its hints in `auth.scope_hints` (4.7). Judge each scope by the most consequential operation that requires it: one operation that can't be undone makes the whole scope `irreversible`. When you're unsure about a scope, leave it out of `auth.scope_hints` rather than guess [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L251) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.splitting-scope-earn` Splitting a scope can earn it a better hint. A personal agent may request `orders:read` freely but ask the user first before requesting a scope that can cancel orders [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L252) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Describing APIs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.clearly-what-operation` Say clearly what each operation does and when to use it, in terms of the user's task [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L255) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-small-whole` Keep them small. The whole description takes room in the model's context, so leave out what personal agents don't need, such as long examples or operations only your own apps call [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L256) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Consent pages

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.start-heading-names` Start with a heading that names the personal agent and says it wants to connect to the user's account, such as "Muse wants to connect to your Example account". Show it on your sign-in page too, before the user signs in, since that's where they decide whether to go on. Word it as connecting, not as "Sign in with Muse", which reads as signing in with a Muse account [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L259) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.user-sign-passkey` Let the user sign in with a passkey or another phishing-resistant method, as on your website. Direct and device sign-in happen on your own pages, so passkeys work there. They can't work with mediated sign-in, where the personal agent collects the credentials. A passkey protects against fake sign-in pages, but not against a user approving a sign-in someone else started, so the advice on this page and for device sign-in still applies [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L260) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.show-personal-agent` Show the personal agent's name and logo, and the domain of its `client_id`. The personal agent chooses its own name, so the domain is what the user can trust [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L261) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.tell-user-continue` Tell the user to continue only if they just asked that personal agent to connect, such as "Only continue if you asked Muse to do this just now." Anyone can start a sign-in and send the user the link, and nothing in the request says who started it. A user who doesn't use that personal agent, or didn't ask, can then decline [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L262) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.show-account-being` Show the account being connected, the requested scopes in plain language, and how long access lasts. Group related scopes rather than listing their names [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L263) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.point-scopes-allow` Point out scopes that allow changes that can't be undone or that show personal data, the scopes your `auth.scope_hints` mark `irreversible` or with `personal_data` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L264) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.poppy-browser-sign` When `poppy:browser-sign-in` allows everything the account can do on your website, say so in plain language, such as "Use the website as you, with full access to your account", and let the user leave it out while approving the rest (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L265) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.issuer-serves-several` When your issuer serves several domains, `poppy:browser-sign-in` signs the browser in on each of them that lists a `browser_session_endpoint`. Name those websites when you ask the user to approve it, such as "Use example.com and example.co.uk as you" (3.2). If any of those websites is unscoped, describe the scope as full access and set `web.unscoped` on every domain (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L266) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.user-already-granted` When the user already granted some of the scopes, show which ones are new, so the user doesn't review the whole list again. A personal agent that needs more access requests every scope it needs again (4.7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L267) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.protect-page-against` Protect the page against cross-site request forgery, and against framing by other sites with `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L268) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.redirect-exactly-match` `redirect_uri` MUST exactly match an entry in the personal agent's `redirect_uris` (4.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L269) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `guide.accept-pkce-s256` Accept PKCE with `S256` only, and reject `plain` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L270) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.return-every-redirect` Return `iss` in every redirect, success or error (4.2). Personal agents reject a redirect without it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L271) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.extra-protection-support` For extra protection, support Pushed Authorization Requests (RFC 9126) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L272) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Device sign-in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.offer-direct-sign` Offer direct sign-in too (SHOULD, 4). Device sign-in is easier to use for phishing [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L275) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.10027-advises-against` RFC 10027 §6.2.1.5 advises against the device authorization grant for sensitive, high-value, or business-critical resources. A company whose accounts hold them, such as a bank, may offer only direct sign-in [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L276) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.follow-best-practices` Follow the best practices for cross-device flows in RFC 10027 §2 (MUST, 4.3): assess the risk before offering device sign-in, and choose mitigations from its §6.1, such as short-lived single-use codes, rate limits, limited scopes, and a consent page that says which personal agent is asking and tells the user to decline a code they didn't ask for [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L277) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `guide.verification-page-issuer` Put the verification page on your issuer's host or your domain, or a subdomain of either. Personal agents don't show a link anywhere else (4.3). If one issuer serves several domains, a page on the issuer's host works for all of them [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L278) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.opening-link-approve` Opening the link MUST NOT approve the request by itself (4.3). The same goes for scanning the QR code. The user signs in and approves on the page [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L279) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `guide.user-confirm-code` Ask the user to confirm that the code on the page matches the one the personal agent shows [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L280) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.return-slow-down` Return `slow_down` to personal agents that poll faster than `interval`, and limit wrong `user_code` entries [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L281) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-expires-short` Keep `expires_in` short, such as 10 minutes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L282) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Mediated sign-in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.rate-limit-attempts` Rate-limit attempts by account, by `client_id`, and by network address, and cap wrong one-time codes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L285) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.require-time-code` Require a one-time code when a sign-in looks unusual, including a personal agent's first mediated sign-in after the user disconnected it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L286) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.return-same-invalid` Return the same `invalid_grant` error for an unknown account and a wrong password, so responses don't reveal whether an account exists [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L287) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.never-store-credentials` Never store raw credentials or codes, including in logs, traces, and idempotency records [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L288) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.tell-user-example` Tell the user, for example by email, when a personal agent signs in [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L289) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Account settings

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `guide.account-settings` In account settings, list each connected personal agent with its name, domain, scopes, and when it was last used [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L292) | SHOULD | company | `signout/disconnect` |
| ! | `guide.offer-control-disconnect` Offer a control to disconnect each one. Disconnecting revokes its refresh tokens, and its sessions continue signed out (5.5). Also invalidate the access tokens issued under them, as RFC 7009 §2.1 allows [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L293) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Browser sessions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.endpoint-host-personal` Put the endpoint on the host personal agents browse when you can. It can be on another host, such as `accounts.example.com`, as long as the session's cookie it sets reaches the pages personal agents browse (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L296) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.make-code-least` Make each code at least 128 random bits, and expire it within 60 seconds [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L297) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.cookie-ties-code` Set the cookie that ties the code to the browser as `__Host-poppy_join=…; Path=/; Max-Age=60; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, with `Max-Age` no longer than the code's lifetime. The `__Host-` prefix keeps other hosts on your domain from setting it, and `SameSite=Strict` keeps a form on another site from sending it (RFC 6265bis) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L298) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.send-page-cache` Send the page with `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, so caches don't keep it, other pages can't frame it, and the page that opened it can't keep a reference to its window (section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L299) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.answer-successful-form` Answer a successful form with `303 See Other`, and a failed one with 400, or 429 when the browser sends too many requests [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L300) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.endpoint-responses-request` Don't log the endpoint's responses or request bodies. They contain browser-session codes [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L301) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-short-lived` Keep a short-lived record for each code: whether it was authorized, for which session and account, and whether it was submitted. A store with a time to live of the code's lifetime works [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L302) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.cookie-session-separate` Use a cookie for the session that's separate from your login cookie, and check it first. After a signed-out join, keep the browser's login cookie. After a signed-in join, clear it, so the browser is signed out when the session's sign-in ends. Section 6 has a table of each case [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L303) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.make-session-cookie` Make the session's cookie `Secure` and `HttpOnly`, and use the `__Host-` prefix when the endpoint is on the host personal agents browse. When it's on another host, such as `accounts.example.com` for `www.example.com`, the cookie can't use `__Host-` and needs a `Domain` attribute. Set `Domain` to the narrowest domain that covers the hosts personal agents need, because `Domain=example.com` is sent to every subdomain, including one an attacker might take over. The join cookie is only read on the endpoint's host, so it keeps `__Host-` either way [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L304) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.look-session-request` Look up the session on each request, so sign-out and scope changes take effect on the website right away [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L305) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Enforcing scopes everywhere

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.apply-same-scope` Apply the same scope rules on your website, APIs, company agent, and live agents. One shared check that every channel calls is easiest to keep consistent. Until your website can, let `poppy:browser-sign-in` stand for the account's full access there (Browser sessions) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L308) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.company-agent-tools` Have the company agent's tools check the token's scopes on every call. Don't rely on the model to decide [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L309) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.give-live-agents` Give live agents' tools the same checks, so a person can't make a change the token doesn't allow (8.11) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L310) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.check-read-write` Check read and write scopes separately. If a write scope also allows reading, say so in its description [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L311) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.website-refuses-action` When your website refuses an action for a missing scope, show an error that names the scopes (SHOULD, section 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L312) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Internal services

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.forward-access-token` Don't forward an access token or Session JWT from one of your services to another [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L315) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.internal-services` Verify them at the edge, then pass the verified `client_id`, session, user ID, account, and scopes to internal services through a gateway or service credentials [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L316) | SHOULD | company | _the tool context carries the verified identity, never the token_ |
| ! | `guide.internal-credentials-used` Internal credentials used for a request shouldn't allow more than the access token does [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L317) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Hosting several companies

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.publish-metadata-issuer` Publish metadata for each issuer at its own URL, such as `https://auth.platform.example/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/outfitters` (3.2). Its `issuer` is the full issuer, and its `protected_resources` lists only that company's storefronts and resources, such as `https://outfitters.example` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L320) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.publish-protected-resource` Publish protected resource metadata on each storefront's domain, with its company's issuer in `authorization_servers` (3.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L321) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.serve-storefront-poppy` Serve each storefront's `poppy.json` on the storefront's own domain. A document redirected to the platform's domain speaks for the platform, not the storefront (3.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L322) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.companies-share-token` Companies can share a token endpoint, servers, and signing keys. Only the issuer decides which company a token belongs to [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L323) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.record-issuer-every` Record the issuer with every session and token, and check it on every request. An access token, refresh token, or Session JWT for Outfitters must not work at Books, even when both are served by the same code [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L324) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.company-records-another` Don't use one company's records for another. A user's sessions, user IDs, and accounts at one company are unknown to every other company the platform hosts [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L325) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: A conversation endpoint at another provider

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.list-conversation-endpoint` List the conversation endpoint in `agent.protocols` in the company's `poppy.json` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L328) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.endpoint-service-resource` Use that endpoint URL as the service's resource identifier, including the tenant path so tokens for different companies have different audiences (RFC 8707 §3). Publish its protected resource metadata at the URL RFC 9728 §3.1 defines: [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L329) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.configure-company-issuer` Configure the company's issuer to issue access tokens for that resource, with the scopes the conversation service uses. Publishing metadata alone doesn't configure the issuer or establish trust between the providers (RFC 8707 §2.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L330) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.personal-agent-discovers` The personal agent discovers the resource and requests its access token from the company's issuer with `resource` set to the endpoint URL, at sign-in or refresh (4.5). The issuer can also list the resource in its `protected_resources` (3.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L331) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.arrange-conversation-provider` Arrange for the conversation provider to validate access tokens from that issuer. For JWT access tokens following RFC 9068, use the issuer's metadata and signing keys and check the issuer, audience, expiry, and other validation rules. Another option is authenticated token introspection (RFC 7662). Enforce scopes and verify the Session header separately, including that the token was issued to the same client (5.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L332) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Offering personal agents less

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.limit-scopes-grants` Limit the scopes it grants by client, as OAuth allows (4.7). It can also leave scopes it doesn't offer personal agents out of `scopes_supported`, as RFC 8414 allows (3.2). When the issuer's metadata can't be tailored, such as a hosted issuer or one shared with other resources, list the scopes personal agents can request in `scopes_supported` of your protected resource metadata instead (4.7). These lists are discovery, not enforcement: agents can request scopes documented by an API or sign-in extension too [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L335) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.refuse-sign-sign` Refuse sign-in, or one sign-in type, to a personal agent with `unauthorized_client` from the grant's endpoint, and keep accepting it for signed-out sessions (4.1). `grant_types_supported` lists the grants every client can see, so a refusal by `client_id` is how you keep direct or device sign-in from some personal agents [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L336) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.turn-sign-every` Turn off sign-in for every personal agent with `auth.disabled`, for example while your issuer serves only other clients, or to keep one identifier across hostname changes before you offer sign-in (3.2). Personal agents don't try to sign in, and still use signed-out sessions. Remove it when you're ready [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L337) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.company-agent-everything` Let your company agent do everything customers can do by phone, as fully as you can, so personal agents have no reason to call [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L340) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.personal-agent-declares` To a personal agent that declares the Links extension, send the pages a reply refers to as links, rather than URLs in `text` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L341) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.personal-agent-declares-2` To a personal agent that declares the Disclosures extension, send notices users need to see, such as allergen or regulatory warnings, as disclosures, and keep them to those. Personal agents decide which to show, and skip ones that read like promotion. Without the extension, put the notice in `text` [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L342) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-what-message` Keep what a message says in `text` and `data`, and use extension content to add to it, so a personal agent that ignores an extension still gets the message (8.4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L343) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.write-whoever-other` Write for whoever is on the other side (8.8). With a personal agent, skip greetings and small talk and keep text short. With the user, use plain sentences, a pace they can follow, and details in `text` rather than only in `data`. In a direct conversation, reply as you would to the customer on your own channels [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L344) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.report-working-true` Report `working` as `true` from the moment you accept a request until you've acted on it and finished replying, so a personal agent that reads until `working` is `false` gets the whole reply (8.7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L345) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.request-company-agent` Set `as_of_request` on each company agent message to the latest request the agent saw when it started the turn, and give the agent the `as_of_cursor` of each personal agent message, so it knows which of its messages a reply answers (8.4). Leave `as_of_request` off messages from people [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L346) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.help-desk-withdraw` If your help desk can withdraw a request for a person, do so on a handoff cancel, so no one is assigned to a conversation that no longer needs them (8.9) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L347) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-conversation-events` Keep a conversation's events for at least 30 days, so a personal agent that reconnects rarely hits `cursor_expired` (8.5) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L348) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.stream-nothing-send` On a stream with nothing to send, send an SSE comment every 15 to 30 seconds, so proxies don't close it (8.6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L349) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.session-signs-answer` When a session signs out, answer requests without an access token on its conversations that used the account with a 401 challenge, including reads of their events, so their account details can't be read signed out (5.5, 8.11). Leave them open, so the user can sign in again and continue, or close them if your policy is to clear everything at sign-out [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L350) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.before-closing-inactive` Before closing an inactive conversation, say so in a message (8.12) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L351) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.send-authorization-event` When you send an `authorization` event, also ask in a message, so a user in a direct conversation sees the request (8.11) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L352) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.sign-verify-user` When sign-in can verify the user, send an `authorization` event (8.11) rather than asking for identifying details in messages, such as a date of birth, part of an account number, or a code sent by text. Sign-in proves who the user is, and it keeps codes and personal details out of messages and model context (Handling secrets) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L353) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.give-people-conversation` Give the people a conversation is handed to (8.9) the same way to ask for sign-in, so they don't fall back to verification questions [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L354) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Excluded tasks and feedback

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.list-tasks-chosen` List the tasks you've chosen not to offer to personal agents, such as ones you allow only in your app for security or regulatory reasons (9.1). Personal agents then stop looking for a way to do them, and don't send feedback about them [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L357) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.write-task-customer` Write each task the way a customer would ask for it, such as "Send a wire transfer" [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L358) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.give-alternative-whenever` Give an alternative whenever there is one. Link to the page, or the screen in your app, where the user can do the task (9.2) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L359) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.serve-excluded-tasks` Serve excluded tasks, skills, and your feedback endpoint from `tasks.endpoint` (section 9). If every Session gets the same response, you can cache it at your edge without verifying the Session header [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L360) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.different-skills-alternatives` To try different skills, alternatives, or feedback endpoints with some users, choose each Session's variant after verifying its Session header, and mark the response `private`. Choose by User ID to keep a user in the same variant across Sessions, or by Session ID to vary it from one Session to the next [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L361) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.different-sessions-different` If different Sessions can get different versions of a skill, give each version its own URL. A personal agent rejects a file whose digest doesn't match the index it got [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L362) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.feedback-report-asks` When a feedback report asks for a task you do offer, answer with an alternative that says how, so the personal agent can finish the task (9.3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L363) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.take-feedback-personal` Take feedback from personal agents at the `feedback.endpoint` in your tasks response (9.3). If your APIs also serve clients that don't read `poppy.json` and you keep a feedback operation for them, say in its description that personal agents use `feedback.endpoint`. Ideally both feed the same place [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L364) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Operations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.approval-actions-business` Ask for approval for actions with a business effect that the user would want to confirm, such as ones that cost money or can't be undone. Don't ask for routine changes the user already asked for in so many words, such as updating a saved address [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L367) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.everything-affects-action` Put everything that affects the action in `terms`. Name its keys after the fields of the request or of your API's resources, such as `order_id`, so personal agents can compare them with what they asked for, and make each value clear on its own, such as an amount with its currency. Personal agents show `terms` to users, or describe them in their own words (Operations 3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L368) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.send-summary-want` Send a `summary` when you want users to read your wording. Write it so it stands alone: what will happen, to what, and any cost, date, or condition. Use bold for what matters most, such as the amount, and keep links out of it. Personal agents that show a summary show yours as is (Operations 3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L369) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.openapi-description-endpoints` Say in your OpenAPI description which endpoints can return `approval_required` or `approval_declined` (Operations 4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L370) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.approval-user-approval` An approval is a user approval, or an agent approval on the user's instruction, and says which in `approver`. Record `approver` and `reference` with the operation, so you can look into an approval with the personal agent's operator later (Operations 8.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L371) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.actions-where-want` For actions where you want to see the user approve, don't return operations. Handle them on your website or in your app until signed user approvals exist (roadmap) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L372) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.choose-expires-kind` Choose `expires_at` for each kind of action. Give the user at least 15 minutes, and longer for terms that don't change, such as cancelling a subscription at the end of the month. Keep it short when you hold something for the user, such as a seat or a sale price. If you don't store operations, you can't hold a price: an approval that arrives after the price changed gets a new revision (Operations 3) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L373) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-record-performed` Keep your record of a performed operation until its approved revision expires, and no longer than you need to. A store with a time to live set from `expires_at` works (Operations 7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L374) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.avoid-storing-operations` To avoid storing operations nobody has approved, compute them from the request (Operations 3). Give a request without an approval a new random `operation_id`, such as `exc_5Rt2`, so a user can repeat an action on purpose. When a request with an approval no longer matches, return the new revision with that approval's `operation_id`. In a conversation, keep the `operation_id` when the user asks for different terms [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L375) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.compute-operations-make` When you compute operations, make the `revision` the expiry as a Unix time and an HMAC-SHA256, with a key kept like your other signing keys, over the `operation_id`, the expiry, the terms in a canonical form such as RFC 8785 whether or not you return `terms`, and who can approve it: the `client_id`, the User ID, and the account when signed in. Include the method, URL, and the parts of the body or tool arguments that affect the action. Leave out the `summary`, so you can reword it [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L376) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.request-comes-back` When the request comes back with an approval, compute the terms again from your current data, such as today's price, then the HMAC. Compare it in constant time and check the expiry. If the price or anything else changed, the HMAC doesn't match, and you return a new revision for the current terms. The revision only shows that the terms changed: always use your current price. If you store operations instead, store each revision's terms with such a fingerprint of the request, so you can check that a request with an approval asks for exactly what was approved (Operations 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L377) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.call-another-system` When you call another system to perform the action, such as a payment processor or a warehouse, derive its idempotency key from the operation ID. A retry then can't perform the action twice downstream either [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L378) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.downstream-call-times` If a downstream call times out, ask that system whether the action happened, using your business reference, before trying again. Until you know, answer retries with 503 and `Retry-After` (Operations 7) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L379) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-record-approval` Keep a record of each approval: the operation, revision, `client_id`, account, and time. It shows what the personal agent stated the user approved (Operations 8.1) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L380) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.approval-website-make` To ask for approval on your website, make the reference in `Poppy-Operation` a sealed copy of the operation and the request's fingerprint, such as a JWS or an HMAC over who can approve it as for the `revision`, so you don't store operations nobody approved (Operations 4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L381) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.keep-recorded-approvals` Keep recorded approvals in the store you use for performed operations, by the account, or by the personal agent's `client_id` and User ID when signed out, with a time to live set from `expires_at`. One record can go from approved to performing to performed (Operations 6) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L382) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.browser-repeats-request` When the browser repeats the request, check it against each unused approval recorded for that account or user as you would check a request that carries the approval: compute the terms and the HMAC again with the approved revision's `operation_id` and expiry. Mark the approval used when you perform the action, so a later request gets a new operation [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L383) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.page-waiting-tell` On the page that's waiting, tell the user the action needs their approval in their personal agent, and offer a Continue button that makes the original request again. A page that polls your own status endpoint can repeat the request itself once the approval is recorded. Don't use operations on the website for an action you can't repeat, such as one behind a single-use form token. Handle its approval yourself instead. Send `Poppy-Operation` on the response to the request itself, including a script's `fetch`, so it works for buttons as well as forms [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L384) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.make-sure-application` Make sure your CDN or web application firewall passes a 403 with `Poppy-Operation` through unchanged. Some replace the body of error responses with their own page or drop headers, and the personal agent then can't find the operation (Operations 4) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L385) | SHOULD | company |  |

## Guides: Error messages

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.keep-error-description` Keep `error_description` and other error text free of account details and other users' data [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L388) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.return-same-error` Return the same error for "doesn't exist" and "belongs to someone else", as `conversation_not_found` does (8.13) [↗](pap-0.4/guides.md#L389) | SHOULD | company |  |
